title: Third-Party Residual Liability
affiliations: Università degli studi di Modena e Reggio Emilia (UNIMORE) - Faculty of Business and Economics and University of Minnesota - Law School

detail.title: Third-Party Residual Liability

publicationDetails.detailsText: Minnesota Legal Studies Research Paper Forthcoming
publicationDetails.journalName: University of Minnesota Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper develops a three-party accident model in which accident risk is jointly affected by the care and activity levels of injurers and victims, as well as by safety investments made by a third party controlling the external risk environment. We consider a third party residual liability (TPRL) rule under which injurers and victims remain liable for losses caused by their negligence, while the third party bears the residual loss when both parties acted diligently or when their negligence cannot be proven. The first step in our analysis is to show that shifting residual liability onto third parties does not undermine the ordinary care incentives of injurers and victims. The paper then examines three additional effects. First, residual liability induces the third party to use its local information to choose safety investments and formulate customized standards of care. Second, access fees and other pricing mechanisms transmit residual accident costs to users, thereby affecting their activity choices. Third, if residual accident risk is shifted from risk-averse parties to a risk-neutral corporate or institutional third party, a risk-spreading surplus is generated. Competition affects the division of the resulting risk-spreading surplus, but not its existence.

title: Site and Scale: Data Centers, Grid Congestion, and Welfare
affiliations: Department of Economics, Applied Statistics, and International Business, New Mexico State University,  and University of New Mexico

detail.title: Site and Scale: Data Centers, Grid Congestion, and Welfare

publicationDetails.journalName: United States Association for Energy Economics (USAEE) & International Association for Energy Economics (IAEE) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Jurisdictions compete to attract data centers, but the price effects of admitting one depend on where the new load lands in the transmission network. We develop a two-node model of large-load entry on either side of a binding transmission constraint. At an import-constrained node, entry raises both the local price and the zonal price at which consumers settle; at an export-constrained node with excess renewable generation, the two prices diverge. We test both cases in Virginia's PJM zones and in ERCOT over 2015-2024, instrumenting data center entry with proximity to the pre-existing long-haul fiber network. We show that the welfare consequences turn on siting, with entry reducing the surplus of existing consumers in the import-constrained market and raising it in the export-constrained one. Because pre-entry congestion is observable, the siting of large loads and the allocation of the transmission costs they create or relieve can be conditioned on local grid conditions.

title: Yuan as an Instrument of Business Adaptation to New Conditions of International Settlements

detail.title: Yuan as an Instrument of Business Adaptation to New Conditions of International Settlements
detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of the Chinese yuan as an instrument of business adaptation to the transforming architecture of international settlements under sanctions, restricted access to traditional payment infrastructure and a gradual shift in the currency structure of cross-border transactions. The aim is to assess the extent to which the use of the yuan enables companies to maintain settlement resilience, reduce dependence on dollar-centric channels and preserve foreign trade activity, while simultaneously creating new constraints related to convertibility, liquidity and reliance on Chinese financial intermediaries. The study relies on comparative and causal analysis, as well as a synthesis of approaches presented in academic and analytical literature. It argues that the yuan should not be viewed as a universal substitute for traditional reserve currencies, but rather as a significant element of a diversified model of international settlements.

title: Algorithmic Targeting for Direct Social Assistance: Eliminating Leakage and Calculating the Vulnerability Gap in Emerging Economies

detail.title: Algorithmic Targeting for Direct Social Assistance: Eliminating Leakage and Calculating the Vulnerability Gap in Emerging Economies
detail.abstract: Evaluating socioeconomic vulnerability represents a critical challenge for social policies in emerging economies, particularly during the macroeconomic transition from regressive universal subsidies to targeted direct cash transfers. The primary obstacle to optimal state allocation is the informational asymmetry within the informal sector, where traditional Proxy Means Testing (PMT) systematically misinterprets depreciating physical assets as generative wealth and fails to account for the structural burden of informal debt. This paper proposes a novel microeconomic framework aimed at accurately detecting multidimensional household vulnerability without penalizing the working poor. We introduce the "Algorithmic Vulnerability Gap" (AVG), a deterministic mechanism that replaces static proxy scoring with a dynamic deficit calculation. The AVG isolates the precise monetary deprivation of a household by deducting its true generative capacity-aggregating declared income, geometrically depreciating assets (δ), and subtracting algorithmically bounded informal debt (Dinf)-from a strictly defined survival baseline. The framework is validated through a dual-methodological approach. First, a macro-scale Monte Carlo simulation (N = 10, 000, 000 households) demonstrates the model's theoretical capacity to eliminate inclusion errors (0% leakage) while dynamically outputting exact sovereign budget ceilings. Second, empirical robustness is verified utilizing the World Bank's LSMS-ISA Harmonised Panel (N = 148, 421 households) of Nigeria. The empirical application successfully translates categorical asset indices into continuous monetary proxies, deterministically calculating exact household deficits and outputting a precise sovereign liability (1.44 billion LCU). The combined results indicate that the AVG architecture provides a mathematically equitable and fiscally impenetrable solution for managing Unified Social Registries (USR).

reference: Banque de France Working Paper No. No. 1057
title: Navigating Shocks: The Ripple Effects of Shipping Route Closures
affiliations: Banque de France

detail.title: Navigating Shocks: The Ripple Effects of Shipping Route Closures

publicationDetails.detailsText: Banque de France Working Paper No. No. 1057
publicationDetails.journalName: Banque de France Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Who bears the cost when a maritime chokepoint is disrupted? Combining ship-level AIS trajectories, port-call logs, freight indices, customs data and Turkish shipment-level data, we document the trade effects of the 2023 Red Sea crisis: seaborne trade between affected country pairs fell, rerouted around the Cape of Good Hope, and recovered within months as freight costs surged, while some exporters shifted persistently toward air freight. We build a quantitative trade model in which freight costs are endogenous to modal and route choice through congestion, a global shipping capacity constraint, and monopoly toll-setting by canal authorities. Calibrated to observed route choices and canal revenues, the model implies that a permanent Red Sea closure lowers global real income only mildly. Because the Suez Canal Authority, pricing to maximize revenue, already captures much of the route's surplus, the loss falls on the toll collector: Egypt forgoes 3.0 percent of real income, almost all of it canal rent, while the large trading economies each lose less than 0.02 percent. A transit fee on the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint without maritime substitutes, instead concentrates losses on the Gulf economies themselves. Whether a chokepoint has substitutes, and who prices it, jointly determine who pays for its disruption.

title: Hawkes-Driven OTC Market Making: Volterra-Riccati Approximation
affiliations: HSBC FX eRisk, Global Markets, HSBC Bank Plc., UK

detail.title: Hawkes-Driven OTC Market Making: Volterra-Riccati Approximation
detail.abstract: We formulate an over-the-counter (OTC) market-making problem in which request-for-quote (RFQ) arrivals are modelled by general Hawkes kernels and fills are controlled thinnings of the exogenous request flow. The modelling choice is motivated by spot-FX RFQ data: after filtering and transforming to seasonality-adjusted RFQ activity time, two-way activity in major currency pairs exhibits large fitted branching ratios and multi-scale persistence. For general Hawkes kernels the control problem is path-dependent: the relevant state contains the order-flow history, or equivalently the forward curve of conditional future RFQ intensities. Exact Markovian lifting is available for exponential kernels, but it becomes high-dimensional for mixtures of exponentials and impractical for long-memory kernels. We therefore develop a hierarchy of Volterra-Riccati approximations. The first level replaces random future request flow by its conditional Volterra forecast; the second adds a covariance correction for intensity uncertainty; the third updates the quote rule with the realized Hawkes memory, or equivalently with the post-request conditional forecast curve. The approximation hierarchy is validated in an exponential Hawkes benchmark, where the exact lifted HJB can be solved numerically. The state-feedback Volterra-Riccati policy closely tracks the exact benchmark, especially in directional regimes, while a memory-free Poisson policy suffers substantial regret. We then apply the same state-feedback rule to a power-law-like RFQ memory model. A directional RFQ burst changes the conditional forecast of future flow and is converted by the continuation-value shadow price into a persistent quote skew. The resulting endogenous OTC quote impact inherits the long-memory decay of the RFQ forecast response and improves inventory and P&L risk control relative to a no-conditioning Poisson benchmark.

title: The Jurisprudence and Ethics of Creation and Destruction: A Generative Relational Perspective

detail.title: The Jurisprudence and Ethics of Creation and Destruction: A Generative Relational Perspective
detail.abstract: Two parties that cannot address one another directly may be reached through others, and the practice is old. What passes along such a path is composed afresh at every relay, so what arrives is not what was sent, and the path also takes time, so what arrives is late. This paper treats the two together. A longer path buys an interval and spends fidelity, and both follow from the same relays, so the interval and the departure cannot be varied independently. Two claims are then advanced. Where nothing corrects the departure, a longer path is worse without qualification, which agrees with what is known of lagged feedback in models of confrontation. Where a correction process operates during the interval, the two effects oppose one another, and the departure surviving at the far end is greatest at an intermediate path length, given here as one divided by twice the product of the correction rate and the latency of a hop. Short paths carry little departure; long paths give correction time to work; the exposed region lies between them. The account then observes that a path carrying an overture carries a threat on the same terms, and that a threat arriving in a departed form is read as evidence of intent, which makes the symmetry worse than a caution. Existing statements that interdependence buys time for negotiation are conceded, and the present account supplies the condition they leave unstated. Nothing here is measured, no empirical claim is made, and the model is offered as a construction whose behaviour is reported.

title: Which Prices Carry the Adjustment? Cross-Item Evidence from a Daily Turkish Price Panel

detail.title: Which Prices Carry the Adjustment? Cross-Item Evidence from a Daily Turkish Price Panel
detail.abstract: When inflation rises, the prices that move go further. This paper asks which prices, using a daily itemlevel panel from a web-scraped Turkish consumer price index: 331 items priced every day for seventeen months, 5,627 item-months, over a range of monthly inflation from 0.87 to 4.84 per cent. Comparing two items facing the same month's inflation, with month fixed effects absorbing the aggregate entirely, the size response is systematically smaller for the item that reprices more often. The interaction of inflation with item flexibility is-0.32 points per standard deviation of flexibility, and runs from-0.32 to-0.39 across four constructions of the flexibility measure, each estimated outside the observations it explains. It survives controlling for item-level volatility, for the mean, skewness and kurtosis of the item's own price changes, and for heterogeneous exchange-rate pass-through, and it strengthens when items at the top of the flexibility distribution are dropped. Identification comes from 331 items within each month, so the estimate does not depend on the length of the sample. A fixed-hazard rule with heterogeneous hazards predicts a small interaction of the opposite sign for this specification, so the estimate is not a foregone conclusion under time-dependent pricing; we nonetheless offer it as a quantitative moment any model of this economy must match rather than as a test between state-and time-dependent pricing, because bracketing it needs a level for the repricing hazard that this source does not measure. Three further results follow from daily observation. A one-point rise in monthly inflation raises the average item's absolute price change by 0.503 points and makes the monthly change 6.1 points more likely to be positive. The cross-item distribution of monthly price changes widens as inflation rises, the ninety-ten spread correlating +0.52, the intermarket counterpart in a third high-inflation economy of the relative-price-variability result established for Israel and for the Polish transition. And because the official monthly price is a geometric mean over the first twenty-four days of the month, we can locate inflation within the month: two days of prices explain 71 per cent of what the completed window explains, and food supplies most of it, reaching 74 per cent of its own terminal explanatory power in two days while clothing contributes essentially nothing early.

title: The Mathematical Failure of Ukraine’s War-Continuation Policy: A Victory-Independent Model of Future-Generation Response-Capacity Depletion
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Mathematical Failure of Ukraine’s War-Continuation Policy: A Victory-Independent Model of Future-Generation Response-Capacity Depletion

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This work is a conceptual and theoretical study and does not involve human participants, personal data, or animal subjects. Therefore, ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This paper argues that Ukraine’s policy of continuing war constitutes a failed policy under the Law of Conservation of Responsibility in Second Physics. The argument is victory-independent: it does not depend on whether Ukraine ultimately wins or loses on the battlefield. Responsibility does not disappear; it is transferred, transformed, and inherited across actors and generations. On this basis, the paper models how continued war shifts responsibility loads to future generations through the following responsibility channels: fiscal debt, reconstruction burdens, infrastructure destruction, environmental damage, mine and UXO contamination, agricultural loss, water-resource damage, educational loss, health-system damage, and human-capital depletion.

The central claim is that, under the assumptions that 𝐷𝑢(𝑡) ≥ 0, 𝐾(𝑡 − 𝜏) ≥ 0, Λ(𝐷𝑢(𝑡)) ≥ 0, the coefficients on the negative terms are positive, and no compensating transformation term is sufficient to offset the accumulated responsibility load, Ukraine’s continuation of war structurally reduces future-generation response capacity, denoted by 𝑄𝑓(𝑡). Here, war damage 𝐷𝑢(𝑡) is not identical with responsibility load; it is mapped into responsibility load through a responsibility-conversion function Λ(𝐷𝑢(𝑡)). When 𝑄𝑓(𝑡) falls to or below the minimum level required for viable national reconstruction,  𝑄min, the policy constitutes a failed policy. This paper neither justifies Russia’s invasion nor denies Ukraine’s right of self-defence. Its question is narrower and structural: whether Ukraine’s continuation of war, especially under external dependence, transfers such a large responsibility load to the future that it constitutes a mathematically failed policy.

title: ADynamic Regional Adjustment and Factor-Specific Mobility: Evidence from Labor, Capital, and Infrastructure Movements across Indian States
affiliations: University of Warsaw

detail.title: ADynamic Regional Adjustment and Factor-Specific Mobility: Evidence from Labor, Capital, and Infrastructure Movements across Indian States
detail.abstract: Regional development depends not only on the mobility of labour, capital, and industrial infrastructure but also on their successful adjustment after relocation. However, existing regional science models primarily explain mobility decisions and spatial interactions while providing limited insight into the dynamic adjustment process. This study develops a Dynamic Regional Adjustment Model that conceptualises regional adjustment through five complementary mechanisms: attraction, regional productivity signals, productive capacity rigidity, resistance, and momentum. A unified nonlinear dynamic econometric framework is proposed and estimated separately for labour, capital, and industrial infrastructure using panel data for 28 Indian states during 2010-2023. The empirical analysis employs IV-GMM, instrument validation, and Difference-GMM estimation to address endogeneity and dynamic persistence. The results demonstrate that regional adjustment is factor-specific rather than uniform across production factors. Labour adjustment is primarily driven by contemporary industrial expansion, capital adjustment exhibits significant historical persistence arising from investment commitments, and industrial infrastructure is characterised by strong productive capacity rigidity associated with accumulated production systems. These findings indicate that regional development depends on the speed and efficiency of post-relocation adjustment rather than mobility alone. By shifting the analytical focus from factor movement to adjustment mechanisms, the proposed framework complements existing migration, gravity, and New Economic Geography models while providing a new theoretical and empirical foundation for adjustment-oriented regional development policy.

title: Integrating Spatial Econometrics and Remote Sensing for Pixel-Level Wind Energy Corridor Identification: Evidence from West Bengal, India
affiliations: University of Warsaw

detail.title: Integrating Spatial Econometrics and Remote Sensing for Pixel-Level Wind Energy Corridor Identification: Evidence from West Bengal, India
detail.abstract: This study integrates remote sensing and spatial econometric techniques to identify pixel-level wind energy corridors in West Bengal, India. Weibull scale (A) and shape (K) parameter rasters at 100 m resolution were combined with Dynamic World land-cover data to evaluate the influence of landscape characteristics on wind potential. District-level zonal statistics were first extracted, and Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Spatial Autoregressive (SAR), Spatial Error Model (SEM), and Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) were subsequently estimated. Global Moran's I (0.723, p < 0.01) revealed significant positive spatial autocorrelation, justifying the application of spatial econometric models. Model comparison indicated that the Spatial Error Model (SEM) provided the best statistical fit among the tested specifications, showing that tree cover and built-up areas are negatively associated with wind potential, whereas flooded vegetation exhibits a positive association. The estimated spatial error coefficient (lambda = 0.945) further confirms the importance of latent regional environmental processes. Based on these findings, a pixel-level wind suitability index was developed to identify potential contiguous wind energy corridors across the state. The results suggest that several districts located in the southern and coastal parts of West Bengal possess relatively high wind energy development potential and highlight the importance of integrated land-use planning. However, the identified corridors should be interpreted as planning-support outputs that require further engineering, environmental, and infrastructure assessments before implementation.

title: Defensive Pessimism: Growth, Culture, and the Survival of Evidence

detail.title: Defensive Pessimism: Growth, Culture, and the Survival of Evidence
detail.abstract:
Successful cooperation can destroy the practice needed to recognize its own failure. I study a growing society in which a common technology raises output and the hazard of an appropriative regime, while a culturally sustained outside practice supplies the counterfactual and operating capacity needed for correction. The key object is cumulative practice erosion measured in breakdown-hazard time. If erosion is less scale-sensitive than breakdown, expected correction is finite; if it is more sensitive, the mean delay is infinite; and equal elasticities produce an exact coefficient boundary. Correction nevertheless remains almost surely eventual unless politics eliminates the outside practice.

The same mechanism creates a mass-share wedge: growth can increase skeptical mass and diagnostic evidence while the skeptics' political share vanishes. Every fixed nonunanimous population threshold is then crossed in finite time. Culture is a stock of epistemic capital rather than an irreplaceable ideology. A fully funded pilot that maintains the complete outside practice can replicate it, but creates a capitalized enforcement and rebuilding liability. Under external commitment, a rolling performance bond forfeited upon cancellation funds that liability, blocking opportunistic repeal while permitting reforms valuable enough to replace the lost experiment.

title: Who Wins? A Distributional Accounting of Bangladesh's Transition from an Agrarian to a Ready-Made Garment Economy

detail.title: Who Wins? A Distributional Accounting of Bangladesh's Transition from an Agrarian to a Ready-Made Garment Economy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to declare
declarations.ethicsApproval: No engagement of human participants, no approval is applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding received

detail.abstract: Bangladesh's transition from a rice-based agrarian economy to a leading apparel exporter is widely presented as a development success. In FY2025-26, the ready-made garment sector earned US$38.70 billion and contributed more than four-fifths of merchandise exports. This article asks a different question: who gained from this transition, who carried its costs, and how can these outcomes be measured? It introduces the LEDGER framework, which examines six dimensions: Land, Effluent, Density, Gender and labour, External accounts, and Rules. The study uses a critical synthesis of peer-reviewed research and institutional evidence on land conversion, water use, environmental pollution, labour conditions, urban concentration, export earnings, and regulatory enforcement. The findings show that Bangladesh's structural transformation remains incomplete. Agriculture's employment share increased while its contribution to gross domestic product declined. Industrial expansion also converted substantial areas of agricultural land, wetlands, and water bodies in Gazipur, Savar, Narayanganj, and the wider Dhaka region. Textile wet processing continued to depend on intensive groundwater extraction, while effective effluent treatment compliance remained limited. Labour-intensive export growth created employment and expanded economic opportunities for women, but real wage erosion, automation, and declining female participation weakened these gains. Export earnings also overstated the value retained within the economy because of imported inputs, statistical discrepancies, and illicit financial outflows. The article argues that the transition represents a distributional transfer rather than an unqualified national gain. Concentrated, priced, and recorded benefits were partly financed by diffuse, unpriced, and poorly recorded social and environmental losses. It proposes twelve reforms to make these losses measurable, visible, and payable.

title: What Moves the Market? A Daily Decomposition of Financial, Foreign, Monetary, Geopolitical, Fiscal, and Labor-Market Information in S&P 500 Returns and Volatility

detail.title: What Moves the Market? A Daily Decomposition of Financial, Foreign, Monetary, Geopolitical, Fiscal, and Labor-Market Information in S&P 500 Returns and Volatility
detail.abstract: Investors, journalists, and policymakers routinely attribute daily stock market moves to a familiar cast of forces: fear gauges, foreign markets, the Federal Reserve, government dysfunction, wars, and the labor market. This paper measures how much each of these information sources is actually associated with daily S&P 500 returns and volatility over January 2012 to August 2026 (3,667 trading days), using only public data: the VIX, overnight returns on the Nikkei 225, DAX, and FTSE 100, 122 Federal Open Market Committee decision days, five verified federal government shutdown episodes together with the daily Economic Policy Uncertainty index, the Caldara-Iacoviello daily Geopolitical Risk index, and weekly jobless claims with monthly employment report days. A six-block decomposition explains 70 percent of daily return variation, but the hierarchy is extreme: implied volatility changes alone account for an R-squared of 0.64 and foreign equity returns 0.37, while the geopolitical, fiscal, labor, and Fed blocks each contribute less than one percent. Conditional effects concentrate instead in second moments: volatility averages 33 percent higher on FOMC decision days, is significantly elevated on employment report and geopolitical spike days, and is statistically indistinguishable from normal during government shutdowns. Around the February 2022 and October 2023 conflict onsets the index rose on the onset day itself and recovered its shallow subsequent drawdown within a month. Lagged values of all six blocks predict next-day returns with an out-of-sample R-squared of minus five percent. The results depict a market that absorbs slow-moving political and macroeconomic narratives into fast market-based prices, prices scheduled information as volatility rather than direction, and leaves no exploitable daily return predictability.

title: HMAT-Net: A Lightweight Hierarchical Multi-Scale Attention Network with Feature Tokenization for Multi-Class Breast Histopathological Image Classification
affiliations: University of Asia Pacific and University of Asia Pacific

detail.title: HMAT-Net: A Lightweight Hierarchical Multi-Scale Attention Network with Feature Tokenization for Multi-Class Breast Histopathological Image Classification
detail.abstract: Breast cancer histopathological image classification is a challenging task due to considerable morphological variations across magnification levels, high visual similarity between tumour subtypes, class imbalance, and the limited capability of conventional convolutional neural networks to capture long-range contextual information. To overcome these challenges, this study presents HMAT-Net, a lightweight hierarchical CNN–attention framework for multi-class breast cancer histopathology classification. The proposed architecture combines a dual-attention convolutional stem for suppressing background interference and staining artefacts, an Attention-Enhanced Multiscale (AEM) block for adaptive multi-scale feature extraction, a lightweight Feature Tokenization Attention Block (FTAB) to model global contextual relationships, and a CBAM-based refinement module followed by combined global average and max pooling to preserve complementary local and global representations. Despite containing only 0.89 million trainable parameters, HMAT-Net achieves a favorable balance between predictive performance and computational efficiency. Experimental evaluation on the BreakHis dataset demonstrates consistent performance across all magnification factors, achieving classification accuracies of 97.53%, 97.58%, 97.75%, and 97.87% at 40×, 100×, 200×, and 400×, respectively, with an overall multi-class accuracy and macro-F1 score of 98.37%. Comparative experiments indicate that HMAT-Net outperforms or matches recent state-of-the-art methods while requiring substantially fewer parameters. In addition, ablation studies verify the contribution of each architectural component, and Grad-CAM++ visualizations enhance model interpretability by highlighting diagnostically relevant tissue regions. These findings demonstrate that HMAT-Net provides an accurate, efficient, and interpretable framework for automated breast cancer histopathological image classification and represents a promising decision-support approach for future clinical validation.

title: The Tell in the Details: Bounded Recall and Credibility in Bargaining
affiliations: University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management, University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management and

detail.title: The Tell in the Details: Bounded Recall and Credibility in Bargaining

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: Within a query-based communication protocol, bounded recall can make communication more credible and improve bargaining outcomes. In a laboratory bargaining experiment, sellers privately observe the realized value and provide uninformed buyers with multi-attribute reports before negotiating price. Bounded seller recall makes consistent misreporting more difficult, thereby (i) increasing truthful reporting, (ii) raising acceptance rates, and (iii) reducing inequality and boosting total surplus. Seller-selected questions weaken these gains. The cognitive burden of sustaining a fabrication thus emerges as a distinct source of credibility, and question-selection authority as a lever of bargaining power.

title: Toward Responsible AI Governance in the Philippine Public Sector: A Literature Review of Ethical Challenges, Policy Gaps, And Governance Frameworks
affiliations: University of Caloocan City, University of Caloocan City, , University of Caloocan City, University of Caloocan City and University of Caloocan City

detail.title: Toward Responsible AI Governance in the Philippine Public Sector: A Literature Review of Ethical Challenges, Policy Gaps, And Governance Frameworks
detail.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming public administration by enhancing decision-making, optimizing service delivery, automating administrative processes, and strengthening evidence-based policy formulation. However, its deployment in government operations raises profound ethical and governance concerns—including algorithmic bias, limited transparency and explainability, blurred accountability mechanisms, data privacy risks, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and inadequate human oversight. While international bodies such as the OECD, UNESCO, and the European Union have developed comprehensive principles and, in the case of the EU AI Act, binding regulatory instruments for responsible AI stewardship, these instruments were designed for jurisdictions with mature regulatory institutions and centralized enforcement capacity that developing country contexts such as the Philippines—a unitary but highly decentralized administrative system—have not yet attained, resulting in continued policy fragmentation, uneven institutional readiness, and regulatory architectures that lag behind technological advancement.

This study adopts a descriptive qualitative research design, drawing on a systematic literature review conducted in full compliance with the PRISMA 2020 framework to synthesize current scholarship on responsible AI governance. Database and institutional-source searching yielded 390 records, of which 29 studies met the final inclusion criteria following title-abstract screening and full-text eligibility assessment. The review critically examines prevailing ethical challenges, globally recognized governance principles, systemic policy and institutional gaps, and established international frameworks applicable to AI-assisted decision-making in the public sector. Integrating these insights with the country's evolving administrative and regulatory landscape—including the National AI Strategy for the Philippines (NAIS-PH), the E-Governance Act (Republic Act No. 12254), and the Philippine Digital Infrastructure and Artificial Intelligence Ecosystem Act (Republic Act No. 12216)—the paper proposes a context-responsive conceptual Responsible AI Governance Framework tailored for the Philippine public sector.

Unlike the OECD Principles, the UNESCO Recommendation, and the EU AI Act, which offer value-based or risk-tiered guidance largely detached from Philippine administrative structures, the distinct contribution of the proposed framework lies in its explicit grounding in domestic constitutional, statutory, and institutional instruments, complemented by staged implementation levels, measurable governance indicators, monitoring and evaluation mechanisms, and a continuous feedback loop suited to a still-evolving and institutionally fragmented Philippine AI policy landscape. The analysis concludes that effective responsible AI governance requires a cohesive, multi-stakeholder approach that integrates ethical safeguards, institutional accountability, legal protections, organizational capacity building, meaningful human oversight, and public trust. The proposed framework serves as a foundational reference for future empirical research and a practical roadmap for policy and institutional reforms, supporting the ethical, inclusive, and accountable adoption of AI across Philippine government agencies.

title: From the Archive to the Interlocutor: Collective Interactive Legacy AI for Cultural, Civic, and Scientific Continuity
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: From the Archive to the Interlocutor: Collective Interactive Legacy AI for Cultural, Civic, and Scientific Continuity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this conceptual study, as it did not involve human participants, personal data collection, or experimental research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes a focused version of the Collective Interactive Legacy AI framework, conceived as an extension of Digital Legacy AI (Frongia, 2026) from the individual to the collective subject. The starting point is the same paradigm shift: not retroactive reconstruction from passive traces, but intentional design grounded in authorization, curated archives, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation. The thesis is that this paradigm concerns not only the biological death of an individual, but can also apply to the ending, transformation, or historical distance of collective experiences: time-limited cultural projects, civic or student movements, research groups, artistic collectives, educational communities, non-profits, events, and local archives. 

We define Collective Interactive Legacy AI as a conversational system grounded in authorization, attributed sources, layered temporality, and archival governance-designed to preserve and keep interrogable over time the intellectual, cultural, ethical, organizational, or procedural legacy of a collective subject. The compact formula is: from the archive to the interlocutor. The aim is not to pretend that a project lives on, nor to build a single artificial voice speaking in place of its members, but to turn a documentary and testimonial corpus into a dialogic memory able to answer future questions while always indicating sources, dates, roles, historical phases, disagreements, and epistemic limits. 

The analysis focuses on three domains: time-limited cultural projects, civic or student movements, and scientific research groups, corresponding to three forms of memory: cultural and transformative, democratic, and epistemic. The main theoretical contribution is to adapt the four-layer identity framework to collective subjects and to introduce a fifth layer, the Internal Tension Layer, which operationalizes dissent as an explicit requirement of the architecture. In the collective case, dissent is not a defect to be erased but a constitutive part of identity.

title: Return to Realism: Declining American Hegemony, Rising China, and the Future of ASEAN Human Rights
affiliations: Mahidol University International College

detail.title: Return to Realism: Declining American Hegemony, Rising China, and the Future of ASEAN Human Rights
detail.abstract: In the late 1980's, the institutionalization of human rights began in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). As Western states promoted progressive values internationally, ASEAN states began liberalizing. In 2009, the ASEAN Intergovernmental Commission on Human Rights (AICHR) was inaugurated. Since then, the AICHR has failed to intervene during many human rights abuses. This article studies the origins of AICHR, noting that with declining American hegemony and rising Chinese influence, Western-style human rights has lost regional promotion. United States (US) realism and Southeast Asian regionalism may leave human rights dependent on ASEAN member states.

title: The Economic Consequences of Insecure Property Rights
affiliations: Hebrew University of Jerusalem - Faculty of Law and Hebrew University of Jerusalem

detail.title: The Economic Consequences of Insecure Property Rights
detail.abstract: Secure property rights support efficient allocation and investment, yet their effects in affluent urban markets remain understudied. We examine Jerusalem properties built on church-owned land under 99-year leases approaching expiration, creating substantial legal and political uncertainty. Using all residential transactions from 2004-2024, we compare nearby properties with secure and insecure rights within the same blocks. Insecure rights reduce transaction likelihood by about 20 percent and prices by 10-15 percent on average, revealing large costs of legal uncertainty. A present-value framework implies that market participants assign a substantial, but far from certain, probability to losing rights. We benefited from valuable comments from David Genesove, Yossi Yakhin and from participants in the annual meetings of the American Law and Economics Association and the Israel Economic Association and the Econ.

title: When Environmental News Fades: Climate, Biodiversity, and the Horizon of Inflation Expectations
affiliations: and University of the Interior of Beira

detail.title: When Environmental News Fades: Climate, Biodiversity, and the Horizon of Inflation Expectations
detail.abstract: This study examines whether environmental-risk news is systematically associated with the term structure of expected inflation and whether this relationship varies across expectation horizons. Using monthly US data from 2000 to 2023, we combine news-based measures of climate and biodiversity risk with model-based estimates of expected inflation from the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland at horizons ranging from one to thirty years. Dynamic autoregressive distributed-lag models reveal a pronounced horizon-decay pattern in the association between climate news and expected inflation. The estimated climate-news coefficient declines monotonically from 0.0158 at the one-year horizon to 0.0008 at the thirty-year horizon, where the relationship is no longer statistically significant. Cross-equation tests provide further evidence of systematic attenuation across the expectation term structure. In contrast, biodiversity news exhibits no statistically significant independent association with expected inflation at any examined horizon, while joint specifications leave the climate-news coefficients largely unchanged. The horizon-decay pattern also persists after controlling for realised year-on-year inflation, although the estimated associations become weaker, particularly at longer horizons. These findings reveal a marked asymmetry in the macroeconomic salience of environmental risks. Climate-related information is associated primarily with movements in shorter-and medium-horizon expected inflation rather than with persistent shifts at the long end of the term structure, while biodiversity-related information exhibits no comparable detectable relationship. The results suggest that the systemic economic importance of environmental 2 risks does not necessarily correspond to the extent to which they are reflected in aggregate assessments of future inflation.

title: Skill-Conditioned Argmax Aggregation for Broker Order Flows: Evidence from Taiwan Equities

detail.title: Skill-Conditioned Argmax Aggregation for Broker Order Flows: Evidence from Taiwan Equities
detail.abstract:
This study explores how different ways of aggregating broker–branch order flow can reshape return predictability in a retail-driven equity market. Drawing on a dataset of roughly 70 million identity-tagged trades from Taiwan between 2018 and 2024—covering 983 branches and 1,863 stocks—we introduce a skill-conditioned argmax aggregation (SCAA) operator that compresses a sparse broker–stock–day panel into stock–day factors. The idea is straightforward: brokers are first scored by rising-edge measures of past trading success for given factors, and the factor vectors of whichever brokers score highest are then inherited. Conventional intensity-based Top-K schemes are identified as a special case in which selection is determined solely by contemporaneous order intensity.

Within this unified framework, the choice of aggregation systematically changes the sign and horizon of predictability. Intensity-selected factors yield short-horizon momentum (RankIC ≈ +0.07 to +0.09), and strategies that simply "follow" historically strong brokers in real time contribute little. Yet when trend-interaction factors are conditioned on success, the sign flips: medium-term reversals emerge instead, with RankIC values around −0.10 at 20 days and −0.14 at 60 days, and the effect grows with the horizon. A plausible explanation is what we refer to as post-discovery attenuation. Once a broker's skill becomes publicly visible and draws attention, crowding tends to erode any remaining trend-following alpha; what is left—often the footprint of earlier information-motivated or inventory-unwinding trades—predicts reversals rather than continuation.

These insights carry over to portfolio construction. In walk-forward XGBoost portfolios under strict retail frictions (10 discrete units, Taiwan costs), models combining SCAA and intensity-based features achieve a mean Sharpe ≈ 3 across eight test windows. Their maximum drawdowns are roughly half those of intensity-only benchmarks, and the strategies outperform a major large-cap Taiwanese index over the same periods. Taken together, the results suggest that aggregation is not merely a preprocessing convention. Rather, conditioning on broker identity and realized skill reshapes the informational content of order flow itself, turning what appears to be a momentum-oriented signal into a more reliable source of medium-term contrarian opportunities.

title: L'Europe unie / United Europe 23/2025: EU and its Neighbours amid AI Transformation and Multi-level Geopolitical Pressures
affiliations: George Emil Palade University of Medicine, Pharmacy, Science, and Technology of Targu Mures, affiliation not provided to SSRN and

detail.title: L'Europe unie / United Europe 23/2025: EU and its Neighbours amid AI Transformation and Multi-level Geopolitical Pressures

publicationDetails.detailsText: L'Europe unie / United Europe; 22/2025; L-ISSN 2743-4052

detail.abstract:
L'Europe unie / United Europe 23/2025: EU and its Neighbours amid AI Transformation and Multi-level Geopolitical Pressures. Print ISSN: 2780-8173;  On line ISSN: 2743-4052; Linking ISSN (ISSN-L): 2743-4052

This peer-reviewed special volume brings together thirteen contributions by scholars representing eleven countries to examine how artificial intelligence and geopolitical pressures are reshaping the European Union and its neighbourhood. Its principal scientific contribution lies in integrating fields often studied separately: digital ethics and emerging technologies; data protection, fintech and financial inclusion; democratic resilience and Russian power projection; and Euro-Mediterranean transformation. The studies combine doctrinal legal analysis, empirical and statistical research, historical process tracing, comparative institutional inquiry and socio-anthropological analysis. They provide original findings on digital trust, deepfakes, neurorights, biohacking, GDPR, European elections, the Budapest Memorandum, hybrid interference, migration and local entrepreneurship. Collectively, they demonstrate that European resilience requires technological innovation to be aligned with fundamental rights, credible security commitments, historical knowledge and inclusive development. 

The volume provides a coherent research agenda and demonstrates L’Europe unie / United Europe’s editorial capacity to publish internationally diverse, methodologically rigorous and policy-relevant scholarship across EU studies, international relations, European law and contemporary history.

Keywords: European Union; EU neighbourhood; artificial intelligence; digital ethics; digital trust; GDPR; neurorights; financial inclusion; democratic resilience; Russian power projection; Budapest Memorandum; European security; Euro-Mediterranean relations; hybrid threats; contemporary history

title: The Generalized St. Petersburg Lottery: Growth-Optimal Analysis Across the (R, p) Plane

detail.title: The Generalized St. Petersburg Lottery: Growth-Optimal Analysis Across the (R, p) Plane
detail.abstract: The St. Petersburg lottery is one point of a two-parameter family: payoff R i with probability (1-p)p i-1. Asymptotically the family has a single coordinate, the Pareto tail index α = log R (1/p); the mean diverges exactly when α ≤ 1, and the lottery posed in 1713 sits on the boundary. The exact optimality identity and the solvency bound generalize verbatim. Replacing the midpoint expansion by a Mellin transform of the harmonic sum proves the constants previously reported as confirmed only numerically. The mechanism is a collision of two simple poles at s =-1, occurring exactly at α = 1-the first rung of a ladder, one collision at every integer α, where the m-th moment diverges marginally and the term b m of the smallstake expansion degenerates into b m ln b. Closed forms follow across the family, with the lattice modulation carried explicitly and evaluated in closed form, of amplitude δ R = 2π/ sinh(2π 2 / ln R). It vanishes at integer prices, so the classical tabulations are exact; over the reals f * 2 C /C does not converge to 1/ √ 2 but oscillates within 2-1/2 (1 ± δ 2), δ 2 = 5.4 × 10-12 , which we detect numerically. The celebrated constants are boundary values: f 0 /f * → α-1/(1-α) and V (f *)/G(f *) →-2(γ + ψ(α))/(1-α), which equal e and π 2 /3 only as α → 1. The same transform delivers every moment of the log-return-on the critical line the moment integrals are k! ζ(k)-and with them the limit law of the realized growth rate: it is asymptotically normal, but the Gaussian regime begins only after a multiple of the doubling time that does not grow with the price, 2.108 τ 2 for the classical game, while the first Edgeworth correction to log-wealth quantiles, 3ζ(3)/π 2 = 0.365 nats, never decays with n. The log-return has an exponential right tail of rate α, so the divergent expectation of the lottery is exactly the divergence of the moment generating function of its log-return at λ = 1. The game is favorable at every finite price throughout α ≤ 1, but the geometric collapse that makes it unplayable-the operative half of the classical resolution-is a knife-edge property of α = 1: one step off the boundary, the price at which the compounding schedule ceases to be executable stops being logarithmic in the demanded execution speed and becomes a power of it. The paradox follows from the expectation diverging marginally, not from its diverging.

title: Anticipatory Financial Anxiety: Behavioral Distortions in Saving and Risk-Taking Among Central Asian Youth
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Anticipatory Financial Anxiety: Behavioral Distortions in Saving and Risk-Taking Among Central Asian Youth

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Anticipated financial anxiety is a relatively recent and highly topical problem of youth, which received little attention regarding behavioral aspects in Central Asian countries. In this work we explore anticipated financial anxietyanxiety caused by the fear of financial failure in future despite the lack of current financial problemsas well as its relation to the financial behavior of youth aged 14-24. For the purpose of the research we used survey data of 531 individuals of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan and examined relations between future-oriented financial anxiety, willingness to engage in risky financial decisions, saving habits, household income level, financial literacy and demographic variables. The results have shown that more pronounced anticipated financial anxiety is significantly related to lower willingness to invest in risky financial instruments. The relation remained statistically significant when controlled for household income level and in the framework of multiple regression analysis, where anticipated financial anxiety was the only significant predictor of willingness to take financial risks. The relation between saving and financial anxiety was weakly positive which means that there may be a certain level of precautionary saving among anxious individuals rather than complete avoidance. No cross-national differences were revealed in the final sample. Preliminary analysis indicated that the relation between anxiety and risk was stronger for females and individuals aged 20-21.

title: Outweighing the Eagle: Can the ASEAN-RCEP Axis Redefine Asia's Trade Future?

detail.title: Outweighing the Eagle: Can the ASEAN-RCEP Axis Redefine Asia's Trade Future?

contentType.other: Working paper on the dynamics of Asian trade.

detail.abstract: This paper critically examines the strategic and economic potential of ASEAN (Association for SouthEast Asian Nations)-RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership) axis in redefining Asia, straight features in an area of shifting global power dynamics and trade belligerence. As the United States-metaphorically represented by the "Eagle" turns more combative and unpredictable in its trade and economic partnerships in the region, the consolidation of ASEAN's centrality within the RCEP and the interrelationships between both presents a compelling counter narrative. RCEP, encompassing 15 Asia Pacific, economic and representing the largest free trade agreement globally by GDP, signifies a structural evolution in regional economic integration, with ASEAN playing an allied coordinating role. This study explores how the ASEAN-RCEP configuration not only enhances intra-Asian trade linkages, but also strengthens regional supply chain resilience, multilateral cooperation, and investment flows in contrast to rising US policy vacillations. Furthermore, the research assesses the extent to which ASEAN's normative leadership and convincing power within RCEP, can shift the locus of global trade governance towards a more Asia centric model. The findings suggest that while the ASEAN-RCEP axis may not wholly outweigh American economic influence in the short term, it certainly possesses the structural coherence and strategic depth necessary to redefine the long-term contours of Asian trade and economic diplomacy.

title: Evidence-Based Legal, Regulatory, and Policy Assessment of Nigeria’s AfCFTA Implementation
affiliations: Ahmadu Bello University

detail.title: Evidence-Based Legal, Regulatory, and Policy Assessment of Nigeria’s AfCFTA Implementation

keywords: and Policy Assessment of Nigeria's AfCFTA Implementation Evidence-Based Legal
and Policy Assessment of Nigeria's AfCFTA Implementation

detail.abstract:
The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement represents Africa’s most ambitious integration initiative, designed to create a single market for goods, services, and digital commerce across 54 nations [TRALAC]. Nigeria, as the continent's largest economy, signed the Framework Agreement on July 7, 2019, and formally deposited its instrument of ratification on December 5, 2020.

However, Nigeria operates a strict dualist constitutional framework. Under Section 12(1) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), no international treaty possesses the force of law locally until it is enacted into domestic law by an Act of the National Assembly (NASS) [NASS].

To navigate this constitutional requirement without causing legal fragmentation, the executive and legislative branches must manage a complex, dual-phase continental treaty architecture. Nigeria has fully ratified the core Phase 1 Protocols (Trade in Goods, Trade in Services, and Rules and Procedures on the Settlement of Disputes) alongside the main framework agreement [TRALAC]. Crucially, the country advanced its digital trade positioning by formally ratifying the Protocol on Digital Trade (DTP) on November 6, 2025.

In contrast, the remaining four instruments—the Protocols on Investment, Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), and Competition Policy (signed in February 2023) and the Protocol on Women and Youth in Trade (signed in February 2024)—remain unratified by the Executive. Under Section 12 of the Constitution, NASS is legally barred from domesticating these four signed protocols until the Executive formally executes their instruments of ratification [NASS].

To bridge this gap between international commitment and domestic enforcement, the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies (NILDS) Division on AfCFTA Law and Policy Programme serves as the primary institutional driver [NILDS]. Operating under advanced legal methodologies, the division provides technical drafting support, policy research, and capacity building to ensure an accurate, constitutionally sound national implementation process [NILDS].

title: Climate Change, Carbon Pricing and Household Inflation Expectations
affiliations: Banque de France, OFCE - Sciences Po, University of Orleans, Laboratoire d'économie d'Orléans, Students and Banque de France

detail.title: Climate Change, Carbon Pricing and Household Inflation Expectations
detail.abstract: This paper studies the effects of climate change and carbon pricing on household inflation expectations, using the ECB Consumer Expectations Survey covering eleven euro-area economies. We find that country-level temperature shocks raise inflation expectations, an effect broadly shared across household types, though largely offset when energy inflation is elevated. Floods, storms, droughts and extreme heat also shape inflation expectations. On the transition side, carbon-driven components of energy and core inflation also raise expectations, consistent with households viewing the green transition as a structural inflationary force. These findings suggest that monitoring climate-related shocks should be part of central banks' assessment of de-anchoring risk and second-round effects on wages and prices.

title: Evidence-Based Review of the African Protocol on Free Movement of Persons, Goods, and Services: Accelerating Trade Mobility and Regional Economic Integration under the AfCFTA
affiliations: Ahmadu Bello University

detail.title: Evidence-Based Review of the African Protocol on Free Movement of Persons, Goods, and Services: Accelerating Trade Mobility and Regional Economic Integration under the AfCFTA
detail.abstract:
The African Union (AU) Protocol on Free Movement of Persons, Right of Residence, and Right of Establishment stands as a vital institutional pillar for the success of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). While the broader AfCFTA agreement has achieved historic political consensus and extensive state participation, the Free Movement Protocol faces a severe implementation deficit. Adopted officially by the AU Assembly on January 29, 2018, in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, the protocol was intended to operate in tandem with the launch of the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM) and the tariff-reduction frameworks of the AfCFTA.

Despite its strategic importance, the Protocol's operational status remains highly restricted. As of the 2025–2026 monitoring period, it has secured only four official state ratifications—Mali, Niger, Rwanda, and São Tomé and Príncipe—falling significantly short of the 15 ratifications required to legally enter into force across the continent. This creates a stark structural asymmetry within the African integration project: while states have committed to a unified continent-wide market for goods and services, the human capital, entrepreneurs, and service providers required to drive that market remain legally bound by restrictive, fragmented national borders.

title: Quantitative Finance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Quantitative Finance
detail.abstract:
Quantitative finance — usually shortened to "quant finance" — is the practice of using mathematics, statistics, and computer code to make decisions about money. Instead of guessing whether a stock will go up because the news looks positive, a quant builds a model, tests it on decades of past data, and lets the math decide.
This paper introduces the full toolkit of modern quantitative finance at a level a Class 12 student can follow. We cover eight big topics: (1) what quant finance actually is and where it came from; (2) the twin building blocks of return and risk; (3) the bell curve and the "fat-tail" problem; (4) diversification and why mixing assets can lower risk; (5) the Capital Asset Pricing Model and beta; (6) options, derivatives, and the Black–Scholes formula; (7) a complete simple quantitative trading strategy; and (8) case studies from the US (Renaissance Technologies' Medallion Fund) and India (algorithmic trading on NSE, Zerodha, Smallcase). Every formula is worked out step by step. The mathematics is entirely within Class 11–12 syllabus.

title: Buyer Power and Product Selection in Interlocking Relationships
affiliations: University Paris-Saclay, INRAE, AgroParisTech, Paris-Saclay Applied Economics, Centre de Recherche en Économie et Management (CREM) and

detail.title: Buyer Power and Product Selection in Interlocking Relationships
detail.abstract: We develop a model of interlocking vertical relationships between manufacturers and retailers, where retailers select which product(s) to distribute. We highlight that an incomplete buyer-seller network may arise for two reasons. When retail substitution and buyer power are high, retailers have incentives to differentiate their product assortments to soften downstream competition. When instead retail substitution and buyer power are low, at least one retailer has an incentive to restrict its assortment to extract rents from manufacturers. We use our framework to provide new insights for competition policy, focusing on horizontal mergers and slotting fee practices.

title: Exploring Potential Strategies for Incorporating Financial Education into the Curriculum of Secondary School in Bangladesh

detail.title: Exploring Potential Strategies for Incorporating Financial Education into the Curriculum of Secondary School in Bangladesh
detail.abstract: The need to provide young people with financial literacy skills is now widely recognized across the world. As financial systems become more advanced and digital financial services become widely available, the ability to manage money, understand credit, and make informed financial decisions has become an essential life skill rather than just a useful ability. For Bangladesh, a nation with a rapidly growing youth population and an ambitious vision of becoming a developed economy, the integration of financial education into the secondary school curriculum represents both a critical need and a strategic opportunity. This assignment explores potential strategies for incorporating financial education into the secondary school curriculum in Bangladesh. Drawing upon international best practices, regional experiences, and the current policy landscape in Bangladesh, it examines multiple approaches ranging from curriculum integration models to pedagogical methodologies, institutional partnerships, and teacher capacity development.

title: Are Firms Embracing ESG Principles Struggling to Retain Investor Confidence Under Economic Policy Uncertainty?

detail.title: Are Firms Embracing ESG Principles Struggling to Retain Investor Confidence Under Economic Policy Uncertainty?
detail.abstract: Investors today rarely look at a company's balance sheet alone. Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria now sit at the heart of how firms are judged, part of a wider move toward sustainable finance. Companies across sectors have responded by building these principles into their operations, treating ESG not merely as a regulatory obligation but as a way to draw capital and strengthen reputation. In South Korea, however, the policy landscape is unusually turbulent. Frequent shifts leave firms facing an unpredictable environment, which raises a pressing question: how does economic policy uncertainty (EPU) shape the performance of the country's ESG leaders? We address this using wavelet-based quantile-on-quantile regression, which lets us trace distributional links across multiple time horizons. The results reveal a relationship that is neither linear nor symmetric. Over short horizons, moderate uncertainty drags on performance, especially in bearish markets. Medium-term effects depend on the quantile, where low uncertainty accompanies stronger returns and high uncertainty does the opposite. Across longer horizons, persistent uncertainty correlates steadily with weaker outcomes for ESG leaders. Together, these patterns suggest that policy instability undermines the nation's progress toward global sustainability targets. Policymakers should therefore work to dampen uncertainty and build a stable setting in which ESG-oriented firms can thrive.

title: Does Disability Reduce the Returns to Livelihood Interventions? Evidence from a Disability-Inclusive Graduation Programme
affiliations: Save the Children International, London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, affiliation not provided to SSRN, BRAC, London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine - International Centre for Evidence in Disability and BRAC

detail.title: Does Disability Reduce the Returns to Livelihood Interventions? Evidence from a Disability-Inclusive Graduation Programme

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study received ethical clearance from Mildmay Uganda Research Ethics Committee (Reference: 0604-2020) and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine Research Ethics Committee (Reference: 22619/RR/21198). Research permit was granted by the Uganda National Council for Science and Technology (UNCST) (Reference: SS529ES). The trial was registered with the Registry for International Development Impact Evaluations (RIDIE-STUDY-ID-626008898983a) and ISRCTN (ISRCTN-78592382).
declarations.funderStatement: We acknowledge financial support from the United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) under the Programme for Evidence to Inform Disability Action (PENDA) (IATI Identifier: GB-EDU-133903-PENDA). Hannah Kuper is funded by a National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Global Research Professorship.

detail.abstract: Support for persons with disabilities (PWDs) in low-and middle-income countries typically takes the form of consumption support rather than economic-inclusion programmes. This is partly because disability is often presumed to lower the returns to productive investment, thereby pitting equity against efficiency. We test this presumption with a clusterrandomised trial of a disability-inclusive graduation (DIG) programme delivered by an NGO in Northern Uganda, which combined asset transfers, coaching, and skills training with disability-responsive adaptations for over 3,300 ultra-poor households. About 18 months after the programme ended, treated households held substantially more productive assets and reported higher income and consumption. These gains were as large for households with a PWD as for those without, and were no smaller when a PWD-rather than another household member-managed the enterprise. The disability-specific adaptations raised programme costs by 17% but lowered measured benefits by only 8%, leaving the benefit-cost ratio above one. Making livelihood programming disability-inclusive can therefore advance equity at little efficiency cost, challenging the presumption that targeting persons with disabilities entails a trade-off between equity and efficiency.

title: A Generative Relational Account of Social Facts: A Preliminary Discussion of Journalism and the Reconstruction of Social Reality

detail.title: A Generative Relational Account of Social Facts: A Preliminary Discussion of Journalism and the Reconstruction of Social Reality
detail.abstract: Journalism is designated to report social facts. Whether that designation can be discharged is ordinarily treated as a question about the reporter, to be answered by care and resources; this paper treats it as a question about the object. On the account developed here a social fact has no presymbolic form, and comes to presence through the relations among situated representations produced under different language systems, so that the reconstruction available to a reader lives in the structure of divergence among them. Two consequences are derived and verified. A reconstruction so constituted survives no coarsening of the representations that carry it, which places balance and consensus summary among the operations that degrade the object they are meant to secure; and fidelity so constituted is a property of an ensemble while obligation attaches to a member, so that no single report discharges it. The paper then returns one negative result and one positive. Criteria requiring an actor to preserve or enlarge a downstream capacity are inoperable, since they require a prediction over an outcome space that cannot be specified in advance, and the same unavailability places the whole burden of prediction on departures from faithful report. What survives is a condition internal to the artefact: the domain of a claim is contained in the relational neighbourhood its material was drawn from, or the extension carries a declared warrant. The paper contributes an ontology in which divergence is constitutive, an assessment condition checkable at the time of writing, a case in which two rationales for one professional practice prescribe opposite remedies, and a formal apparatus whose propositions were checked before being stated.

title: Generalized Mean Absolute Directional Loss for Machine Learning Trading Models
affiliations: , University of Warsaw - Faculty of Economic Sciences and University of Warsaw - Faculty of Economic Sciences

detail.title: Generalized Mean Absolute Directional Loss for Machine Learning Trading Models
detail.abstract: The article presents and evaluates a custom loss function designed specifically for machine learning models used in algorithmic trading. Regardless of the selected asset class and the level of model complexity, the proposed Generalized Mean Absolute Directional Loss (GMADL) function produces superior results and has better numerical properties during optimization than classic regression and classification based loss functions. Better results correspond to higher risk-weighted returns based on buy and sell signals derived from forecasts generated by models trained using GMADL. In practice, GMADL improves model evaluation by aligning the learning objective with trading performance rather than generic error minimization or simple directional accuracy. Through additional parameterization, GMADL provides a flexible mechanism for adjusting the loss's sensitivity to different return magnitudes, which affects model evaluation consistency across various market regimes. This improves the selection of model configurations that are more consistent with performance-based criteria. Moreover, the implementation uses robust machine learning tools, including frameworks for hyperparameter tuning, architecture testing, and walk-forward optimization, to provide robust and scalable model evaluation across real-world financial data from different asset classes.

title: The Political Economy of Infinity Economies: Ownership, Power, and Governance in AI-Driven Generative Systems
affiliations: African Research Network (ARN)

detail.title: The Political Economy of Infinity Economies: Ownership, Power, and Governance in AI-Driven Generative Systems
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence, generative technologies, decentralized infrastructures, and digital platforms is transforming the foundations of economic organization. While the emerging literature on post-scarcity and the Infinity Economy highlights the growing importance of knowledge, automation, and AI-driven value creation, comparatively little attention has been devoted to the political economy of these transformations. This article investigates how ownership, power, and governance are being reconfigured as generative systems increasingly shape production, exchange, and wealth creation. Drawing on political economy, institutional economics, AI governance, and complexity theory, the paper examines the concentration of algorithmic power, the ownership of data and computational infrastructures, the governance of decentralized autonomous systems, and the implications for economic inequality and democratic accountability. It argues that the transition toward Infinity Economies is not solely a technological transformation but an institutional and political one. Without inclusive governance mechanisms, digital commons, and equitable ownership arrangements, AI-driven abundance may coexist with unprecedented concentrations of economic and political power. The article proposes a governance framework based on distributed ownership, algorithmic transparency, democratic oversight, and planetary responsibility, providing a foundation for future research on the political economy of generative systems.

title: Who Adopts Crypto-Assets? Evidence from Five European Economies
affiliations: University of Luxembourg, Polytechnic University of Milan - Politecnico di milano and Polytechnic University of Milan - Politecnico di milano

detail.title: Who Adopts Crypto-Assets? Evidence from Five European Economies

declarations.funderStatement: The contribution of Luca Pennella was funded by the PayPal-FNR PEARL Chair in Digital Financial Services, FNR grant reference 13342933/Gilbert Fridgen, and by the FutureFinTech National Centre of Excellence in Research and Innovation, FNR grant reference 16570468, with the support of Luxembourg’s Ministry of Finance.

detail.abstract: Crypto-asset adoption combines elements of digital innovation, financial decisionmaking, and asset-specific knowledge. Understanding which individual characteristics most clearly distinguish adopters is therefore important for research on digital finance, retail investing, and investor protection. Using a harmonized survey of 5,125 respondents in France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom, this study examines the individual-level correlates of having ever owned crypto-assets, defined as current or past ownership. We estimate multivariate logistic regressions combining socio-demographic characteristics, traditional financial-market participation, perceived and objective crypto knowledge, information environments, technology attitudes, and urbanization controls. The results show that traditional financial asset ownership, perceived crypto knowledge, and objective crypto knowledge are among the strongest correlates of adoption. By contrast, broad technology-readiness measures do not add robust explanatory power once financial participation and crypto-specific knowledge are taken into account. Television as a crypto-information source is negatively associated with realized ownership, while digital and specialized sources are more closely associated with the broader outcome of crypto engagement, which also includes future acquisition intentions. Crosscountry heterogeneity remains, with higher adoption rates in Spain and the United Kingdom relative to Germany. Overall, the evidence suggests that crypto-asset adoption in these five 1 European economies is more strongly associated with retail financial participation and crypto-specific knowledge than with generalized technological affinity. These findings are relevant for financial education, investor protection, and risk communication in digital finance.

title: Monitoring The Situation on the Oil Market in H1 2026
