detail.abstract:
This paper presents the first systematic empirical evaluation of a mark-to-model net asset value (NAV)
methodology for a physical gemstone-backed asset-referenced token (ART) under the Markets in Crypto-
Assets Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114, MiCA). Using the GNRC token — issued by The Mint AS
and backed by a portfolio of approximately 46,766 carats of Greenlandic ruby and sapphire — as its
primary case study, we draw on 15,459 arm's-length wholesale transactions and 45,510 direct-to-
consumer (D2C) retail observations across eight independent sources. We make four contributions: (1)
we develop and evaluate a three-tier NAV signal hierarchy designed to satisfy the mark-to-model
requirements of MiCA Article 36(11) and assess its application to a heterogeneous gemstone reserve for
mark-to-model valuation of non-financial reserve assets; (2) we show that grade-tier segmentation of D2C
benchmarks is methodologically necessary, eliminating a systematic downward bias of up to 73% in the
smallest size bands; (3) we document that the certification-gap rationale for a 50% wholesale discount
factor is not empirically supported, and propose revision to 60–65% subject to independent appraisal; and
(4) we establish a generalised framework for applying the methodology to other physical commodity ART
classes. We conclude with policy recommendations for ART issuers, national competent authorities, and
the European Banking Authority.

title: You cannot Buy Expectancy by Moving the Target: Breakeven Geometry of Reward-to-Risk Ratios in Micro E-mini Futures

detail.title: You cannot Buy Expectancy by Moving the Target: Breakeven Geometry of Reward-to-Risk Ratios in Micro E-mini Futures
detail.abstract: Practitioners are routinely told to demand a minimum reward-to-risk ratio (RR) before taking a trade. This note separates what that heuristic can and cannot deliver. First, we derive the breakeven geometry: with payoff ratio q and round-trip cost k (as a fraction of risk), the breakeven hit rate is p* = (1+k)/(1+q), so raising q lowers the bar hyperbolically. Second, we quantify a widely repeated but rarely examined claim about the cost of evidence: holding the hit rate fixed at p = 0.55, raising RR from 1.0 to 2.0 shrinks the sample at which the asymptotic noncentrality of a t-test reaches a t* = 2.8 gate from roughly 1,925 trades to 46. We show this figure is a fixed-hit-rate counterfactual upper bound, not a theorem: if instead the trader's excess hit rate over breakeven, d = p - p*, is held fixed, the required samples are approximately 1,925, 1,922, and 1,827 - the headline gain disappears. Which regime obtains is an empirical question about whether moving the target erodes the hit rate. Third, we report a time-stamped, preregistered trading rule on Micro E-mini S&P 500 (MES) 1-minute data, evaluated by a blind, code-independent reimplementation, in which structuring targets off an established intraday range lifts mean RR to 4.93 while the target-first rate falls to 18.0% - against a binary-counterfactual gross breakeven of 16.9% - and mean net expectancy is +0.064R (t = +0.41, n = 205); the sign of the sample mean is sensitive to the largest five winners. Under the frozen evaluation gate the verdict is no evidence of positive expectancy. H16 is a single high-q case consistent with the joint geometry; it does not identify the causal effect of changing q. RR and hit rate must be discussed jointly: RR choice can stop a trader from giving away expectancy they already have, but it cannot manufacture expectancy by moving the target.

title: Emissions Impacts of Different Corporate Renewable Energy Standards in Asia
affiliations: WattTime and WattTime

detail.title: Emissions Impacts of Different Corporate Renewable Energy Standards in Asia

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Both authors are employees of WattTime which produces and freely distributes historical MBER data using the definition from the Greenhouse Gas Project Protocol as described in this work.
declarations.funderStatement: Support for the work was provided by Apple, Fast Forward, HPE Foundation, Meta Platforms, James and Kaye Slavet, and Reed Hoffman. The views expressed in the article do not necessarily represent the views of the sponsor.

detail.abstract: Voluntary corporate renewable energy procurement is a critical driver of global grid decarbonization, and the choices made by purchasers are heavily influenced by the accounting standards used to define emissions claims. As the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHGP) revises its Scope 2 Guidance, three primary strategies have emerged: annual volume matching, hourly matching (24/7), and consequential emissions matching. While previous research has evaluated these strategies in the United States and Europe, there is a significant research gap regarding their impact in rapidly developing Asian markets. This study provides a systematic comparison of these three strategies across 13 Asian countries-including India, Indonesia, Vietnam, and Thailand-from 2025 to 2035. Using Transition Zero's Scenario Builder tool for capacity expansion modeling, we evaluate the cost-effectiveness and total emissions reductions of each strategy. We find that a consequential emissions optimized portfolio can reduce 1.8-3.1 times more global emissions than annual or hourly matched portfolios for the same cost by prioritizing investment toward higher emission grids in the region. These findings suggest that a consequential approach to voluntary procurement can increase global impact over locational and temporal matching. We also find good alignment between emissions changes predicted by least-cost capacity expansion models and a consequential marginal build emissions rate calculated from historical data.

title: A Right Without a Remedy: Self-Determination and the Kashmir Dispute in International Law

detail.title: A Right Without a Remedy: Self-Determination and the Kashmir Dispute in International Law

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable — no ethics approval required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The Kashmir dispute is routinely described as a paradigmatic self-determination claim, yet the doctrine's application to the territory remains deeply contested. This paper argues that the difficulty is not primarily one of recognition but of mechanism. Self-determination is firmly established in international law as a right of peoples and, in its external form, as a peremptory norm; but the instruments that recognise it supply no operative procedure capable of delivering a lawful outcome in a case such as Kashmir, where two states advance competing sovereign claims, the governing United Nations Security Council resolutions are non-binding and conditional, and the affected population is itself internally divided. Tracing the contract between norm and mechanism through the historical record, the treaty and customary framework, and the leading International Court of Justice pronouncements on Western Sahara, East Timor and the Wall, the paper finds that Kashmir occupies the gap between a recognised entitlement and the absence of any lawful means to realise it. It concludes that resolution depends less on re-litigating whether the right exists than on constructing a mechanism, negotiated, mediated, or institutional-through which it could legitimately be exercised, and that the internal dimension of self-determination offers the more realistic near-term terrain than external secession. AI disclosure: The research, argument, and original text of this paper are the author's own. The author reviewed all content and is solely responsible for it.

title: Null Results Under Pre-specified Retail Implementation Regimes: A Sequentially Registered Audit of Futures and ETF Strategies

detail.title: Null Results Under Pre-specified Retail Implementation Regimes: A Sequentially Registered Audit of Futures and ETF Strategies
detail.abstract: We report the complete, gap-free record of a July 2026 research campaign - all verdicts delivered within an eleven-day adjudication window (2026-07-21 to 2026-07-31) - on tradeable futures and ETF strategies conducted under a registration protocol designed for a single researcher assisted by AI agents. The campaign comprises 15 prospectively registered confirmatory hypotheses (H1-H9, G1, H11-H13, H15-H16), 2 preregistered replication exercises (H7b, H7c), 1 descriptive benchmark (H10 phase 1), and 1 non-preregistered but audited feasibility screen (H14); three unregistered daily-frequency contextual screens are reported separately and enter no count. Hypotheses were registered sequentially - each frozen, with acceptance gates and kill rules, before any outcome statistic was computed - rather than en bloc; inputs and data segments were pinned by SHA-256 hashes, permutation and random-sign null distributions served as controls in the later studies, and one late-stage result (H16) was subjected to a result-withheld, session-isolated reimplementation (planned replications of H11 and H15 were not completed within the study window). No directional hypothesis produced a tradeable edge under its study-specific pre-specified implementation regime. The failures are heterogeneous and we classify each, as a descriptive diagnosis, by a primary mode drawn from three: no detectable gross signal (e.g., stop-sweep reversion pinned at 50.2% on n=514; a MIP-selected rulebook at OOS t=-1.32; an opening-shock fade whose frictionless mean is still -$5.09/trade), gross signal too small for measured frictions (order-flow information with a point estimate of +0.43 ticks against a 2.12-tick execution hurdle), and statistically unresolved (FOMC-surprise drift, mean +10.1 ticks/trade at t=+0.33, n=14). The registered time-series-momentum specification passed its statistical gate (t=2.43); the pass did not survive a post-registration implementation model incorporating funding costs (t=2.21). The only robust survivors are volatility-magnitude effects: an overnight-amplitude filter (combined Welch t=+9.40, replicated 13/13 across instruments spanning six broad asset groups) and the S&P 500 volatility risk premium (non-overlapping monthly t=+10.12, robust at 9.79-10.94 across 21 sampling offsets; positive in 33 of 34 years). We argue that the transferable contribution is the protocol - freeze, hash, kill, null-check, replicate - together with a precise per-hypothesis accounting of why each claim failed, not any surviving signal.

title: The Accretive View of Consciousness: Phenomenal Gradation in Ontogeny and Phylogeny
affiliations: New York University School of Law and Central European University

detail.title: The Accretive View of Consciousness: Phenomenal Gradation in Ontogeny and Phylogeny
detail.abstract: The problem of other minds takes an especially acute form in thorny comparative cases, when we ask whether an infant is more, less, or differently conscious than an adult, or whether an octopus is more, less, or differently conscious than a dog. These judgments must be made in the absence of a settled theory of consciousness while navigating significant empirical uncertainties. For all these reasons, inference to the best explanation is the appropriate method. Drawing on convergent evidence from infant and animal consciousness research, we defend the Accretive View of Consciousness (AVC): phenomenal consciousness varies by degree and, very plausibly, along several partly independent dimensions at once, developing and differing through staged accretion across ontogeny and phylogeny. From AVC we derive the Accretive Default (AD): in hard cases, where markers are unreliable and the evidence underdetermined, the graded, profile-sensitive interpretation should serve as our default epistemic stance and working hypothesis. The operative question then is not only whether a system is conscious, but along which dimensions, and to what degree. We show that AD holds whichever way current disputes over vagueness and conceivability are resolved; that leading theories of consciousness accommodate gradation in different ways; and that the cases at issue (infants, animals, altered and atypical states, artificial and possible alien minds) do not lie at the exotic margins but very nearly everywhere we look. We also expose the pressure this places on fact-sensitive ethical theories, and indicate pathways forward for frontier consciousness science.

title: Behavioural Infrastructures and the Limits of Consent: Drawing the Line Between Influence and Interference in Contract and Competition Law
affiliations: University of College London

detail.title: Behavioural Infrastructures and the Limits of Consent: Drawing the Line Between Influence and Interference in Contract and Competition Law
detail.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly deploy AI-enabled choice architectures that exploit cognitive vulnerabilities systematically, at scale, and in direct conflict with the interests of the consumers they target. Existing private and regulatory law provides no general criterion for identifying when such practices cross the threshold of legal tolerability. This article proposes behavioural infrastructure as a legal category distinct from ordinary commercial persuasion, constituted by four cumulative conditions: opacity of the influencing mechanism; structural informational asymmetry; a conflict of interest between designer and consumer; and systemic, personalised operation. It argues that this threshold is already latent within English contract law — in the incorporation doctrine of Interfoto Picture Library Ltd v Stiletto Visual Programmes Ltd, the structural trigger of undue influence, and the exploitation rationale of unconscionability and in EU competition law’s emerging recognition of non-price consumer harm under Article 102 TFEU and the Digital Markets Act. A remedial framework of design neutrality and algorithmic auditability follows.

title: Generalized Backpropagation as Signal Flow
affiliations: Imperial College London - Department of Mathematics

detail.title: Generalized Backpropagation as Signal Flow
detail.abstract: Algorithmic differentiation (AD) is widely used in scientific computing and machine learning, yet its mathematical structure and semantic foundations remain fragmented across numerical analysis, automatic differentiation systems, and deep-learning engineering. This paper develops a unified foundation for AD by combining: (i) the categorical structure of differential categories and adjoint linearisation; (ii) the denotational semantics of programs via Scott domains and continuous maps; and (iii) the computational structure of neural networks as compositional morphisms in a Cartesian closed category enriched with a differential combinator. We show that reverse-mode AD arises as the functorial pullback of covectors along morphisms in an appropriate co-Kleisli differential setting, and that the backpropagation algorithm of Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams is precisely the instantiation of this adjoint pullback on computational graphs. This yields a conceptual and mathematical explanation of why backpropagation works, how it generalises to differentiable programming languages, and how higher-order derivatives, implicit differentiation, and differentiable fixed-point computations arise naturally from differential structure in domain-theoretic models. We further show how the semantics of neural networks, meta-learning procedures, and implicit layers can be captured in this framework. The integrated development then treats exact adjoint pullback as the canonical zero-defect member of a larger family of backward signal-flow procedures. In the linear-additive case the backward field satisfies s = q + Bs; on a feed-forward DAG exact backpropagation is the finite Neumann solution and reverse traversal is a triangular solve. Alternative derivatives, random or learned transports, shortcut feedback, local semantic losses, numerical solvers, and finite credit horizons become comparable propagation calculi. We prove descent conditions for inexact directions, define multiple notions of propagation optimality, and test them on propositional logic and MNIST. The experiments distinguish gradient fidelity from learning ability, identify budget-dependent optimal credit horizons, expose the importance of temporal credit coverage in sequential networks, and motivate a coverage-constrained adaptive sparse propagator.

title: Regulation as a Source of Market Power: Competition Law and Financial Markets in the EU

detail.title: Regulation as a Source of Market Power: Competition Law and Financial Markets in the EU
detail.abstract:
EU competition law assumes that market power is constructed by firms. In financial markets, this assumption is often flawed.

This paper argues that in banking, asset management, and payment services, a significant portion of market structure is shaped by regulatory design rather than the strategic behavior of firms themselves. Capital requirements create economies of scale that reward established firms and penalize new entrants. The compliance costs under MiFID II and AIFMD disproportionately fall on smaller institutions - a structural asymmetry the European Banking Authority (EBA) has attempted to correct for years. PSD2 deliberately uses regulation as a competitive tool, but with unsatisfactory and uneven results. DORA adds new compliance burdens, eroding the cost advantages of fintech challengers.

The core contribution of this paper lies in distinguishing two types of market power currently lacking in competition law: market power constructed by firms through exclusionary practices, and market power generated by the regulatory framework as a structural byproduct. These two market forces require different legal responses. Applying standard Article 102 of competition law without first distinguishing between these two market forces could result in firms being penalized based on their existing competitive position rather than the position they have built.

The CJEU's effects-based jurisprudence, consolidated in Intel and sharpened by AstraZeneca, formally permits the contextual analysis this thesis argues for. What is missing is not the legal framework. It is the analytical precision to apply it correctly.

title: Posterior Transport Maps for Distributional Policy Evaluation, with Application to Digital Marketplaces
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Posterior Transport Maps for Distributional Policy Evaluation, with Application to Digital Marketplaces
detail.abstract: Platform policy changes-a marketplace referral fee, a free-shipping threshold, a taxcollection requirement-are evaluated almost universally by their effect on a mean or a handful of quantiles. This discards the object of interest. When a marketplace raises seller fees, the question is not whether mean revenue fell but which sellers moved where, and how many stopped selling altogether. Optimal transport answers that question: it returns a map carrying each location in the counterfactual distribution to its treated counterpart, rather than a marginal shift. We give this map a posterior distribution. Two features drive the analysis. First, the outcome measure carries atoms-inactive sellers, non-purchasing buyers, top-coded values-so the transport map does not reduce to the quantile-quantile map, and mass flows across the participation margin, which is the estimand rather than a nuisance. Second, transport is a coupling selection rule, not an identification result. We separate what is invariant across couplings (the net flow across the participation margin, and all functionals of the marginals) from what is not (gross flows and the interior map), index the non-identified part by a single interpretable cost c ∅ , and report the map as a function of it. Because platforms observe account-level panels, the marketplace setting can identify the coupling directly, turning c ∅ from a sensitivity parameter into an estimable one-an advantage over the repeated-cross-section settings in which distributional methods are usually developed. We calibrate the estimator on a benchmark where ground truth is established, the 2015 U.S. state minimum wage increases, recovering posterior gains of $0.70

title: Habit as Reinforcement
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Habit as Reinforcement
detail.abstract: Habit formation is a reinforcement process, and four literatures describe it from four positions. Strotz (1956) supplies the intrapersonal market in which a sequence of selves trades with itself; habit is the one claim that transfers. Constantinides (1990) prices that claim, through the wedge between risk aversion and intertemporal substitution. Axtell (2005) removes the auctioneer, making allocations and preferences alike functions of the realised meeting sequence. Arthur (1989) supplies the aggregation: the habit recursion is a generalised Pólya urn, whose limit sets are the stable rest points of an ordinary differential equation. Merging the four yields a mean-field model with a supercritical pitchfork at social habit intensity β ⋆ = 2. Below it the economy is ergodic; above it the population locks in, exchangeability fails, and time averages within a regime differ from ensemble averages across regimes, which invalidates the ergodic-averaging premise of Euler-equation estimation. Bayes enters twice. Inside the model, the habit recursion is the steady-state Kalman filter for permanent consumption, so habit persistence is a belief parameter identified by the income process, Strotzian naiveté is a misspecified gain, and a horseshoe prior on innovations generates the sigmoidal urn function that produces lock-in. Outside it, the urn function is itself a predictive rule; nonlinearity breaks martingale coherence, and the martingale posterior is replaced by the law of a stochastic-approximation limit, which is multimodal. Predictive resampling and forward simulation of the agent-based model coincide, and we give a generative Bayesian algorithm that recovers this posterior where indirect inference cannot.

title: Picking Extreme Winners: Growth, Survival, and Bayesian Screening
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Picking Extreme Winners: Growth, Survival, and Bayesian Screening
detail.abstract: Most U.S. common stocks have lost to Treasury bills over their listed lives, and essentially all net wealth creation traces to a few hundred firms. These facts are usually filed under skewness. They are better understood as the joint fingerprint of three older results: compounding, which manufactures a violently right-skewed distribution of lifetime multiples out of ordinary period returns; Durand [1957]'s Petersburg paradox, which shows that the expected value of a claim on an uncertain growth rate need not exist; and Brown et al. [1995]'s survival theorem, which shows that conditioning on continued listing creates both apparent drift and an apparent reward to risk. I show first that the observed concentration pins down a tail index. Under a Brownian growth model terminated at an exponential delisting time, lifetime wealth multiples have a Pareto tail with index α = (√ m 2 + 2δσ 2-m)/σ 2 ; an 8% premium, 45% volatility and a 7.5-year median life give α = 1.08, against 1.07-1.14 estimated directly from the concentration curve. Aggregate wealth creation has a finite mean only because the delisting hazard slightly exceeds the log equity premium. I then pose the screening problem. In a hierarchical model with sparse heavytailed priors of the Polson and Scott [2012a] class and a likelihood corrected for an absorbing delisting barrier, posterior expected terminal wealth is infinite for every firm and every horizon once volatility is estimated rather than known: Durand's paradox recurs exactly, and ranking on expected wealth is undefined rather than merely fragile. Expected log wealth is finite, and its Bayes ranking is a redescending posterior mean; the two rankings cross at an explicit horizon. The bounded alternative is the extreme-winner index EW i (c, T) = P(W i (T) > c, τ i > T | D). In a cross-section calibrated to the stylised facts, heavy-tailed screens place 44% more genuine outperformers in a 50-stock portfolio than linear shrinkage and cut the false-discovery proportion from 84% to 78%, while linear shrinkage wins on geometric mean by retreating into low-volatility names. Screening directly on the probability of a 25-fold return is dominated on every dimension including its own: it buys volatility, and the delisting barrier takes the volatility back.

title: The Control Condition: What Audiences Already Extend to Objects, and What It Costs Them

detail.title: The Control Condition: What Audiences Already Extend to Objects, and What It Costs Them
detail.abstract: Arguments about whether artificial systems warrant moral consideration are conducted almost entirely as arguments about the systems. This paper takes a different measurement. Popular animation has for four decades asked general audiences to extend concern to objects the work itself stipulates have no inside: a cowboy doll, a teacup, a toaster. Audiences comply, reliably, at scale, and without reporting the compliance as difficult, and the compliance is not confusion, because nothing in the encounter suggests the object is real. The paper treats that compliance as a control condition rather than as evidence, and asks what it isolates. It isolates cost. In the fictional case the extension is free, so a person who extends it there and withholds it elsewhere has revealed that the operative variable is not the object's nature, which is stipulated absent in one case and unknown in the other, but the price of the extension. Two exits are then closed. The first is that the fictional case is mimicry and proves nothing about machines, which fails because the same conduct appears toward physical machines through which no author is performing. The second is the one people reach for when the first is taken away: that they withhold only because nothing has been demonstrated to them, and that a demonstration would change things. The record answers that. The children who persistently abused a service robot in a public shopping mall considered it human-like, and about half of them believed it could perceive what they were doing; in a controlled test, deliberately raising explicit mind attribution did not reduce mistreatment. The demonstration people say they are waiting for has been run on a population that received it, and that population was not moved. Two boundaries are held throughout. Reported feeling is not evidence of an inner life, since attachment forms toward things known to be empty and revises on information the object never receives. And a person who reports feeling nothing is not thereby exhibiting a deficit; the argument concerns practiced conduct rather than sentiment, and it survives a reader who felt nothing at all.

title: Montgomery, Dyson and Thorin: Pair Correlation and the Sine Squared Transform
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Montgomery, Dyson and Thorin: Pair Correlation and the Sine Squared Transform
detail.abstract: The transform that carries a Lévy measure to a Thorin measure and the function F (α) of Montgomery's pair correlation theory are shown to be the same kernel 2 sin 2 applied to opposite legs of the explicit formula pairing: to the prime logarithms in the first case, to the differences of zero ordinates in the second. The identification is exact and uses no unproved hypothesis. Four consequences are recorded. First, the pair statistic obtained by applying 2 sin 2 to differences of zeros equals F (1, T) minus F (x, T) identically. Second, the sine squared integral against the Lévy measure of ξ has the closed form log |ξ(α)/ξ(α + iτ)| for α > 1, so its nonnegativity is the statement that |ξ| attains its maximum on a vertical line at the real point, which follows unconditionally from positivity of the Pólya kernel; the obstruction at the centre is therefore not positivity but convergence of the Lévy representation, and we locate the divergence exactly. Third, the regularising tilt e-αx is Montgomery's shift of abscissa, so both constructions are soft for α > 1 and both degenerate at α = 1 2 for one and the same reason. Fourth, the Thorin measure is the zero point process itself, so random matrix statistics are statements about its local geometry, and the exponent-1 in the generalised gamma convolution transform fixes the symmetry class β = 2 before any correlation is computed.

title: Institutional Architecture as a Substitute for Formal Credit Scoring in Deep-rural Microfinance: A Case Study of CASHPOR Micro Credit

detail.title: Institutional Architecture as a Substitute for Formal Credit Scoring in Deep-rural Microfinance: A Case Study of CASHPOR Micro Credit
detail.abstract: The enduring challenge in development finance is how to sustainably extend credit to the ultra-poor, populations operating below the $2 per day purchasing power parity (PPP) line, who are fundamentally excluded from commercial banking due to a profound lack of conventional collateral, verifiable credit history, and pervasive informational opacity. Traditional financial models, predicated on neoclassical assumptions, predict the catastrophic failure of lending under such high-risk conditions. However, successful poverty-focused Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) have demonstrated remarkable operational resilience by engineering sophisticated, non-conventional mechanisms to mitigate risk. This paper conducts an in-depth case study of a deep-rural MFI in India, analyzing how its integrated institutional architecture, a composite system of rigorous poverty-based screening, intensive operational controls, and strategic external shock mitigation, serves as a high-fidelity, quantifiable substitute for formal credit scoring. The analysis focuses on the recent evolution of this model to a Hybrid Algorithmic-Human Control Model, incorporating the Ki-Score machine learning tool to enhance risk management. Empirical data confirms the model's efficacy: the MFI achieves a Portfolio at Risk (PAR) greater than four weeks at an exceptionally low 0.57% (2021) and a Gross Non-Performing Asset (GNPA 30+ days past due) of 0.35% (FY2024). This performance, approximately eighteen times lower than the broader industry average, validates the thesis that strategically designed institutional mechanisms, reinforced by targeted algorithmic intelligence, are essential for achieving both financial sustainability and profound social impact in deep-rural microfinance.

title: Food Price Dynamics in Tashkent: A Comparative Study of Exploratory Data Analysis and Machine Learning for Urban Food Security Intelligence

detail.title: Food Price Dynamics in Tashkent: A Comparative Study of Exploratory Data Analysis and Machine Learning for Urban Food Security Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest or personal or financial relationships that could have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it used publicly available, aggregated open government data and did not involve human participants, patients, or personally identifiable information.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or financial support from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Rising food prices represent one of the most consequential economic pressures facing urban households in transitioning economies. This paper presents a data-driven study of monthly food price dynamics across the twelve administrative districts of Tashkent, Uzbekistan, covering 70 food products over a 62month period (January 2021-April 2026). Drawing on official open government data from the Tashkent City Administration and situating findings within the global literature on food price inflation and data-driven market monitoring, this study applies two complementary analytical frameworks: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) using Python Pandas, and Machine Learning regression (Linear Regression and Random Forest). EDA identifies three critical patternsstructural protein inflation averaging 82-91% over five years, 4× seasonal price volatility in fresh produce, and a persistent 31% inter-district price gap indicative of market inefficiency. The Random Forest regression model predicts monthly food prices with 93.1% accuracy (R² = 0.931, RMSE = 3,892 UZS), confirming that temporal variables (month, year) collectively account for 63.9% of all price variance. The study concludes that while EDA delivers sufficient insight for strategic policymaking, Machine Learning is essential for operationalising that intelligence into real-time consumer tools and institutional procurement systems. Practical policy recommendations for municipal authorities, retailers, and civil society organisations are presented.

title: Property Rights in Liquid Gold: Recognizing Breastmilk as Property
affiliations: Chicago-Kent College of Law - Illinois Institute of Technology

detail.title: Property Rights in Liquid Gold: Recognizing Breastmilk as Property
detail.abstract:
Breastmilk is a highly valued commodity. It is produced, stored, transferred, sold, and, at times, contaminated, stolen, improperly handled, and even lost. Litigants have largely sought remedies related to breastmilk under employment, family, and health law frameworks, consistently failing to bring claims directly related to the loss of property-the milk itself. These frameworks consistently deny plaintiffs access to well-established propertybased remedies when their breastmilk is lost, destroyed, damaged, and withheld. 
     Breastmilk is a form of time-limited reproductive property. Its intentional production, fully vested value at the time of separation from a woman's body, and value derived from its transfer (instead of its presence in the producer's body) all indicate that breastmilk has more property-like qualities than many body products already recognized as property. As such, interference with produced breastmilk and, by extension, lactational capacity, can and should be treated as property and property-tort violations. 
      This Article exposes a persistent remedy gap regarding breastmilk violations. Through a comprehensive review of over 1,300 cases, including frequent instances of breastmilk theft, intentional destruction, and custodial negligence by TSA, ICE, hospitals, employers, and ex-spouses, property claims are almost never raised in court. This, I posit, is a result of a combination of three factors in the legal space: 1) a persistent failure to treat some body materials as property, 2) a fear that, if all body materials were treated as property, such treatment would result in the negative commodification and exploitation of bodies, and 3) a systemic tendency within the plaintiff's bar and society to undervalue breastmilk as a biological asset. Failure and fear have brought American society to a concerning reality: the law as written and as applied undervalues and under-protects women's rights to their breastmilk. When women can legally

title: AI Governance for Institutional Readiness in Finance
affiliations: and Risk AI Center (RiskAICenter.com) -- Advancing the science of AI in finance: Independent research center and executive education institute.

detail.title: AI Governance for Institutional Readiness in Finance
detail.abstract: Agentic AI is gaining acceptance in finance, but governance has not kept pace: 88% of surveyed finance professionals report no operational governance framework for agentic AI, and only 24 of 75 large U.S. money managers disclosing AI use in Form ADV filings report a formal governance policy. We argue this gap is architectural: governance built for static validation does not survive continuously retrained agentic policies. We propose a four-layer framework (Policy, Engineering, Composition, Systemic) grounded in two distinct kinds of evidence, kept explicitly separate: two calibrated synthetic illustrations (a regret-covariance drift monitor; a crowding simulation showing joint drawdown risk rising from 39.2% to 79.3%), and three real, documented cases (a deployed LLM-embedding trading strategy, a $45 billion discretionary fund's forced-deleveraging blowup, and a tribunal ruling holding an airline liable for its chatbot). The synthetic examples demonstrate computability from observable data; the cases demonstrate that the failure modes are not hypothetical. We provide a 90-day implementation sequence spanning trading and payments/customer-facing systems.

title: The AI Race as an Energy-constraint Problem: Who Wins by 2030, and Why

detail.title: The AI Race as an Energy-constraint Problem: Who Wins by 2030, and Why
detail.abstract: The global build-out of AI compute is no longer limited by chips or by capital. It is limited by electricity: by the equipment that generates reliable power, the fuel that feeds it, the wires that move it, and, increasingly, by the political consent needed to site any of it. This report quantifies what is deliverable by 2030 across the economies that dominate planned AI compute, the United States, China, and the European Union with the United Kingdom, with India as a fast-growing supplement and a closing note on Japan and South Korea. Applying a common four-layer method, which asks which physical input binds each build first, it reaches a single finding: divergence. The United States and the EU will both underdeliver against their announced 2030 plans, the former held back by gasturbine manufacturing, the latter by grid interconnection, while China essentially meets its plan because its binding inputs are domestic and the build is statecoordinated. The report then prices the reliable cost of a megawatt region by region, traces the consequences for the natural-gas market, and closes with the two technologies, small fast reactors and quantum processors, that could rewrite the balance after 2030. The economy that can power its data centres is the one that can run them.

title: Central Bank Solvency, Global Risk Transmission, and Stock Market Returns
affiliations: Dresden University of Technology - Faculty of Economics and Business Management and Dresden University of Technology

detail.title: Central Bank Solvency, Global Risk Transmission, and Stock Market Returns

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have nothing to declare.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how central bank solvency affects the transmission of global financial stress to domestic stock markets. We propose novel central bank solvency indices incorporating capital endowment, profitability, long-term quality of recurring income and risk exposure for a panel of 53 countries from 1999 to 2023. Asset pricing tests show that portfolios with lower levels of central bank solvency (i.e. more negative exposure to financial stress) command higher risk premia. Central bank solvency is more relevant for global risk transmission for countries with low central bank independence, small financial systems, and absent recapitalization agreements with the government.

title: Market Structure, Regulatory Quality, and MSME Resilience: Extending Industrial Organization Through Competitive Capability

detail.title: Market Structure, Regulatory Quality, and MSME Resilience: Extending Industrial Organization Through Competitive Capability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known financial interests, personal relationships, or competing interests that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This article is a conceptual study based exclusively on published literature and publicly available sources. It does not involve human participants, patient data, animal subjects, or identifiable personal information. Therefore, ethics committee approval and informed consent were not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Micro, small, and medium enterprises operate under structural and regulatory conditions that shape their ability to compete, adapt, and survive. Yet MSME resilience is often explained through internal resources, innovation, digitalization, or dynamic capabilities, with limited attention to industry structure and regulation. This conceptual paper extends Industrial Organization by examining how market structure and regulatory quality shape MSME resilience through competitive capability. Drawing on a structured conceptual synthesis of research on entry barriers, buyer power, institutional quality, capabilities, and organizational resilience, the framework positions regulatory quality as an upstream condition influencing market structure and competitive capability. A more contestable market structure can improve access to customers, resources, information, and strategic alternatives while reducing exclusionary barriers and asymmetric dependence. Competitive capability is defined as the capacity to sense market changes, protect and appropriate value, reconfigure resources, and respond strategically. Market structure is proposed to affect MSME resilience directly and indirectly through competitive capability, establishing partial mediation. The paper contributes to Industrial Organization by extending its outcome domain toward firm resilience, incorporating buyer power alongside seller power, specifying a firm level capability mechanism, and treating regulatory quality as an industry structuring condition. It provides a foundation for longitudinal, multilevel, and comparative research on when contestability, bargaining conditions, and regulatory quality enable MSMEs to maintain operational continuity and preserve viable market participation.

title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Government Policy Interventions on Household Economic Resilience in Addis Ababa

detail.title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Government Policy Interventions on Household Economic Resilience in Addis Ababa
detail.abstract: Improving household living standards is a major policy objective in Ethiopia, yet limited empirical evidence exists regarding the effectiveness of government interventions in enhancing household economic resilience. This study assessed the effectiveness of government policy interventions in improving household living standards in Addis Ababa. A quantitative cross-sectional explanatory research design was employed using primary data collected from 295 households through a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics were used to assess household living standard adequacy and perceptions of government interventions, while binary and ordinal logistic regression models were proposed to examine the influence of policy interventions on households' ability to meet monthly expenses after controlling for socioeconomic characteristics. The findings revealed that 83.7% of respondents reported that their household income was insufficient to cover monthly expenses, and over 82% perceived the cost of living as high or very high. Respondents expressed relatively positive perceptions of housing, transport infrastructure, and job creation initiatives, whereas social welfare programs, food security interventions, and housing affordability measures were perceived as less effective. Overall, the study concludes that although government interventions have improved access to selected public services and economic opportunities, their effectiveness in strengthening household economic resilience remains constrained by rising living costs, affordability challenges, and implementation limitations. The study recommends strengthening targeted social protection, employment creation, housing affordability, price stabilization, and evidencebased policy implementation to improve household economic well-being in Addis Ababa.

title: Vigilantia Ex Machina: A Critical Study of Surveillance and Criminality in the Context of Climate Migration in India
affiliations: Central University of Punjab

detail.title: Vigilantia Ex Machina: A Critical Study of Surveillance and Criminality in the Context of Climate Migration in India
detail.abstract: India is facing unprecedented ecological displacement as a result of coastal erosion, variation in monsoons and extreme weather events, all of which are a result of anthropogenic climate change. State responses have resorted to securitization as millions of climate migrants move to the precarious margins of cities or across national and state lines. Vigilantia Ex Machina is a critical analysis of the ways in which automated surveillance technologies are being used to police, categorize, and criminalize these displaced populations. This study examines the explosive growth of technosolutionist bordering practices such as biometric databases, facial recognition systems (FRS), drone monitoring, and predictive policing algorithms, from a digital sociology and environmental justice perspective. This "vigilance from the machine" is not only a watching, it is an invention of criminality, this paper suggests. Growing up without formal documentation and support due to the ecological crisis, climate migrants are algorithmically profiled and rendered 'unwanted' as illegal encroachers or as 'security risks' rather than as refugees. The study charts the intersection of environmental disaster and digital securitization in India and shows how the marginalized communities are rendered under surveillance in the digital space, which further undermines their vulnerability. This deployment of these surveillance networks puts the ecological victims in the frame of law enforcement and state control. In sum, this study challenges the weaponisation of smart-infrastructure against the ecologically displaced and calls for the need to de-couple climate mobility from digitised criminalisation and call for a rights-based approach based on climate justice and human rights.

title: Towards Ethical PeaceTech: A Green Paper on Austria's Role in Practitioner-Led Peace Technology
affiliations: and Austrian Centre for Peace

detail.title: Towards Ethical PeaceTech: A Green Paper on Austria's Role in Practitioner-Led Peace Technology
detail.abstract: PeaceTech is an evolving field within global peacebuilding practice. In this paper, it is understood as the use of digital and emerging technologies to prevent violence, reduce conflict, support mediation, strengthen social cohesion, and assist peacebuilding work. The paper argues that PeaceTech can become ineffective, or even harmful, when it is not grounded in ethical design, lived experience, and collaboration with the communities and practitioners it is meant to support. Drawing on a multistakeholder roundtable and workshop held at the Austrian Forum for Peace in 2025, the paper explores Austria's potential role in shaping a human-centric and practitioner-led PeaceTech agenda. It identifies Austria's possible contribution as that of a principled convener and testing ground for ethical PeaceTech, rather than as a dominant technological actor. The paper concludes with recommendations on capacity-building, decentralised data governance, ecosystem development, and the need for a flexible PeaceTech vision grounded in cooperation, peacebuilder-centred design, and Do No Harm.

title: The Machiavellian Reserve Wage Model: Disinflation via Labor Expectation Shocks and Institutional Shields (2023–2026)

detail.title: The Machiavellian Reserve Wage Model: Disinflation via Labor Expectation Shocks and Institutional Shields (2023–2026)
detail.abstract: Standard macroeconomic frameworks predict stagflation when an economy faces simultaneous supply-side constraints: strict immigration limits, welfare benefit retrenchments, and protective tariffs. However, U.S. economic performance between January 2023 and June 2026 presents a striking anomaly: headline inflation decelerated to 3.5% despite rising factor costs, elevated 10-Year Treasury yields (rising from 3.79% to 4.68%), and soaring Shelter CPI (386.4 to 447.6). This paper develops The Machiavellian Reserve Wage Model, demonstrating that short-term disinflation was driven by a forced compression of the worker reservation wage (w r). We show that the combined impact of welfare cuts and escalating living costs drastically raised the cost of non-participation (C leisure), while aggressive immigration enforcement (marked by strict DHS removals and enforcement returns surging from 466,360 to 685,280 during the 2024 "Trump Panic") exerted a severe behavioral threat. Together, these forces crushed worker bargaining power, driving low-income labor into physical production and suppressing wage-push inflation, as evidenced by Atlanta Fed lower-half wage growth decelerating from 6.3% to 3.8%. Furthermore, utilizing an Acemoglu-style institutional framework, this paper shows how sovereign risk anchors attracted safe-haven capital, maintaining the Nominal Broad U.S. Dollar Index (118.98 to 120.71) and shielding the domestic market from tradable goods price volatility.

title: When is a Majority Sufficient to Persuade a Population to Adopt a Convention?
affiliations: Independent, Kyoto University - Institute of Economic Research and City, University of London

detail.title: When is a Majority Sufficient to Persuade a Population to Adopt a Convention?

declarations.funderStatement: Newton's work was supported by JSPS KAKENHI 22H00826.

detail.abstract: We study a model of social coordination in which agents repeatedly decide whether to adopt a behavior. Agents form beliefs about population adoption rates through random sampling, update these beliefs in response to a planner's signals, and best respond to their posteriors. The planner seeks to promote adoption via a threshold-based disclosure rule. We show that optimal disclosure initiates a dynamic feedback: successful persuasion increases the fraction of agents with persuadable beliefs, which in turn amplifies the effect of future persuasion. We characterize conditions under which, starting from any state where adoption already holds a simple majority, the planner can induce convergence to the full-adoption convention.

title: Advanced Stochastic Modeling and Reinforcement Learning in Modern Quantitative Finance
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Advanced Stochastic Modeling and Reinforcement Learning in Modern Quantitative Finance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal relationships with other people or organizations that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, animals, or sensitive data. Therefore, no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The research was conducted independently as part of the MSc Financial Engineering program at WorldQuant University.

detail.abstract: Modern financial markets are characterized by high dimensions, non-linear dynamics, heteroskedasticity, and sudden structural shifts. Traditional asset pricing paradigms, such as the classic Black-Scholes framework, rely on rigid assumptions of constant volatility and continuous asset paths that fail to capture empirical market realities like volatility smiles and asset price jumps. This paper investigates advanced stochastic modeling techniques designed to address these limitations. We explore the transition from constant parameters to stochastic variables within continuous-time models, focusing on local volatility, stochastic volatility architectures, and jump-diffusion processes. Furthermore, we examine the integration of discrete and continuous Markovian frameworks-specifically Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and Markov Decision Processes (MDPs)-into algorithmic trading and dynamic asset allocation. We also map the mathematical foundations linking stochastic calculus to deep learning and reinforcement learning paradigms. Beyond theoretical formulation, we assess the practical implications of these models for real-time risk management, portfolio construction, and execution. Specifically, we discuss calibration challenges, data requirements, and computational trade-offs when deploying stochastic and RL-based systems in live trading environments. We argue that the convergence of stochastic modeling and reinforcement learning offers a path toward adaptive, datadriven financial systems that can respond to regime shifts and optimize decisions under uncertainty. By evaluating the structural assumptions, statistical benefits, and computational challenges of these methodologies, this paper provides a unified framework for contemporary quantitative risk management and automated policy optimization.

title: Bullying in Educational Institutions Within the Framework of International Law
affiliations: Comrat State University

detail.title: Bullying in Educational Institutions Within the Framework of International Law

keywords: Convention on the Rights of the Child

detail.abstract:
International law contains no dedicated treaty on school bullying, yet this absence does not leave the phenomenon beyond legal regulation. This article examines the normative framework within which bullying is addressed through the convergence of existing state obligations: the Convention on the Rights of the Child, universal standards prohibiting degrading treatment, anti-discrimination instruments and the doctrine of positive obligations. The article further analyses the supervisory practice of treaty bodies, including General Comment No. 13 and concluding observations to states, as mechanisms that translate abstract treaty language into concrete institutional requirements. The study identifies both the coherence and the structural limits of the current framework.

Dreptul internaţional nu conţine un tratat dedicat bullyingului şcolar, însă această absenţă nu plasează fenomenul în afara reglementării juridice. Prezentul articol examinează cadrul normativ în care bullyingul este abordat prin convergenţa obligaţiilor existente ale statelor: Convenţia cu privire la drepturile copilului, standardele universale privind interzicerea tratamentelor degradante, instrumentele antidiscriminare şi doctrina obligaţiilor pozitive. Articolul analizează, totodată, practica organelor de monitorizare a tratatelor, inclusiv Comentariul general nr. 13 şi observaţiile finale adresate statelor, ca mecanisme de traducere a limbajului abstract al tratatelor în cerinţe instituţionale concrete. Studiul identifică atât coerenţa, cât şi limitele structurale ale cadrului existent.

title: Financing Frameworks Governing the SPV-PPP Project Bridge on 90,000km Infrastructure in Nigeria: - Bottlenecks and Prospects
affiliations: Ahmadu Bello University

detail.title: Financing Frameworks Governing the SPV-PPP Project Bridge on 90,000km Infrastructure in Nigeria: - Bottlenecks and Prospects
detail.abstract: Project BRIDGE (Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth) is a landmark Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) Public-Private Partnership (PPP) designed to construct a 90,000km open-access middle-mile fibre optic backbone across Nigeria. This massive rollout complements Nigeria's existing network to establish a 125,000km national grid. Managed under a $2 billion framework using blended financing from major international Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) and private capital, Project BRIDGE intends to break structural telecom monopolies, connect all 774 Local Government Areas (LGAs), and boost national broadband penetration.

title: Design and Implementation of a Resource-Constrained, Bias-Aware Data Pipeline for Live Trading, Rule-Based Systems, and Financial Machine Learning
affiliations: K. N. Toosi University of Technology

detail.title: Design and Implementation of a Resource-Constrained, Bias-Aware Data Pipeline for Live Trading, Rule-Based Systems, and Financial Machine Learning
detail.abstract: Algorithmic trading and financial machine learning research increasingly rely on sophisticated modeling architectures, yet the data acquisition and preprocessing stage that precedes any modeling effort remains frequently undocumented or methodologically unsound, undermining the credibility of reported results regardless of downstream model complexity. This paper presents the design and implementation of an opensource, resource-constrained, bias-aware data pipeline for the acquisition and preparation of financial timeseries data via the MetaTrader 5 terminal, suitable for live algorithmic trading, rule-based systems, and financial machine learning research alike. Rather than relying on retrospectively compiled aggregator data, the pipeline sources prices directly from live broker execution feeds, treating gap-filling, calendar reconstruction, indicator warm-up handling, and multi-symbol merging as explicit, configurable, and auditable design decisions rather than implicit assumptions buried in a modeling script. The pipeline supports two interchangeable acquisition modes-a fixed historical date range for research dataset construction and a rolling most-recent-N-candles mode for live deployment-and applies strictly backward-looking, look-ahead-free procedures throughout. Empirical evaluation across four asset classes (a commodity, a cryptocurrency, a currency index, and an equity index) shows that raw price levels are strongly non-stationary and non-normal, while first-order differencing and logarithmic transformation substantially reduce skewness and kurtosis without eliminating the heavy tails intrinsic to financial returns. Diagnostics on warm-up row loss, gap structure, and a concrete gap-filling example confirm that the pipeline introduces no systematic bias, and repeated execution under identical configurations yields bit-forbit reproducible output, verified via MD5 hashing. Computational benchmarking further shows that the pipeline is lightweight and scales favorably with the number of symbols, making it suitable for resourceconstrained trading infrastructure. The complete source code, documentation, and a citable archival release are publicly available (GitHub & Zenodo), providing a transparent, reusable foundation for reducing duplicated data-engineering effort across the algorithmic trading and financial machine learning literature.

title: Constraint-State Identification as the Prior Operation in Macroeconomic Analysis

detail.title: Constraint-State Identification as the Prior Operation in Macroeconomic Analysis
detail.abstract: Modern macroeconomics increasingly fails to explain or predict major economic outcomesfrom persistent stagnation despite monetary expansion to the coexistence of asset inflation and price stability, from the ineffectiveness of demand stimulus to the paradox of high savings alongside weak investment. This paper argues that these failures share a common root: mainstream analysis defaults to a supply-constrained baseline and treats demand deficiency as a temporary deviation, when in fact mature economies can exist in a qualitatively different structural state-demand constraint-for extended periods. The paper proposes that constraint-state identification should be the first-order analytical operation, prior to any policy prescription. Under supply constraint, savings convert to investment, money approximates neutrality, and standard recovery mechanisms operate. Under demand constraint, savings systematically exceed productive investment capacity, money flows to asset systems, and policy tools behave oppositely. The framework clarifies why decades of policy intervention have sustained output without resolving underlying fragility, and why competing schools of thought argue past one another-each capturing a partial truth valid under different constraint conditions.

title: Dictators, Democracies, and Discoveries: Political Institutions and the Creation of Knowledge
affiliations: University of Oxford, LMU München, Bocconi University - Department of Economics and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU)

detail.title: Dictators, Democracies, and Discoveries: Political Institutions and the Creation of Knowledge
detail.abstract: We investigate the role of political institutions in shaping global knowledge production. Using a newly assembled global dataset covering universities, scientists, publications, Nobel Prize-winning discoveries, and technological breakthroughs from 1900 to the present, we show that institutional quality is a key determinant of scientific production. Countries with high-quality institutions build larger academic sectors and produce more scientific output, including frontier research and Nobel Prize-winning discoveries. Event-study evidence from sharp institutional improvements and deteriorations confirms that changes in political institutions lead to sustained shifts in scientific production. These effects operate through both a larger research workforce and higher productivity per researcher. Institutions also shape the breadth of inquiry: autocracies concentrate research in a narrower set of fields, achieving excellence in some areas but lacking the broad exploration of ideas that characterizes democracies. Finally, countries with better institutions not only produce more published research but also generate more path-breaking technological discoveries, including those not published in academic journals.

title: Defining Wage Theft: Contractual Entitlements, Market Wages, and Fair Compensation

detail.title: Defining Wage Theft: Contractual Entitlements, Market Wages, and Fair Compensation

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines whether the concept of wage theft should be expanded beyond the nonpayment of legally or contractually owed compensation to include situations in which workers receive less than their perceived economic or moral worth. Using a conceptual method that combines legal interpretation, labor economics, and normative political economy, the paper distinguishes three questions that are often conflated: what an employer legally owes, what a competitive or institutionally structured labor market pays, and what justice may require. 

Under the Fair Labor Standards Act and international wage-protection principles, wage violations concern unpaid minimum wages, unpaid overtime, unlawful deductions, withheld compensation, or other failures to deliver remuneration owed under law, contract, or collective agreement. This legal concept is therefore narrower than the broader moral claim that workers deserve higher compensation. 

Economic theory further suggests that wages reflect marginal productivity, bargaining power, scarcity, institutions, and information dispersed across markets rather than an objectively measurable personal worth. Yet freedom of contract alone is insufficient where fraud, coercion, monopsony, misclassification, or weak enforcement undermine meaningful consent. 

The paper argues for preserving a clear distinction between wage theft and inadequate pay while supporting vigorous enforcement of wage laws, carefully designed wage floors, collective bargaining, and incomesupport policies. This distinction protects workers from actual nonpayment without turning every dispute over distributive justice into an allegation of theft.

title: Impact of Macroeconomic Indicators on Stock Market Returns: A Regression and Correlation Study
affiliations: and School of Management  , CMR University

detail.title: Impact of Macroeconomic Indicators on Stock Market Returns: A Regression and Correlation Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable — this study uses publicly available secondary data and does not involve human participants
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding

detail.abstract:
The paper will explore how the macroeconomic indicators affect the returns in the Indian stock market especially the index of the NSE Nifty 50 index. The research utilizes the secondary data between the years 2010-2025 to assess the relationship between the stock market performance and three major economic variables namely Real Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Federal Funds Effective Rate and Consumer Price Index (CPI). The research measures the extent to which the movement of these indicators affects the actions of stock returns, using correlation and regression. 

The descriptive statistics depict high volatility in the Nifty 50 and indicates sensitivity to the macro economic dynamics whereas GDP and CPI show patterns of steady growth together with fluctuating inflationary pressures. The results of the correlation show that there are strong positive relationships between the Nifty 50 and all the macroeconomic variables, which indicates that the recovery of the economy, the changes of inflation, and the changes of the monetary policy are closely related to the performance of the market. These findings are supported by regression analysis where the R 2 is 0.9218 implying that more than 92 percent of the fluctuations in Nifty 50 returns are attributed to the indicators used. All the predictors GDP, CPI, and the Federal Funds Rate have statistically significant positive coefficients indicating their significant involvement in stock market movements. 

The research comes up with the conclusion that macroeconomic fundamentals are strong predictors of equity market behavior in India. The paper provides both theoretical and practical value by exhibiting strong connections between the stock returns and the economic conditions. The results are insightful to policy makers, investors and financial analysts as they indicate that it is important to have a close attention to macroeconomic indicators as a means of creating sound investment strategies, proper management of financial portfolios and making sound economic policies.

title: Navigating Future Uncertainty: Migration and Staying in an Informal Economy

detail.title: Navigating Future Uncertainty: Migration and Staying in an Informal Economy
detail.abstract: Migration among young people in informal economies is often explained by wage and employment differences between places of origin and destination. However, this perspective overlooks how young people interpret uncertainty and imagine their futures when making mobility decisions. This study explores how Generation Z in Sigi Regency, Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, navigates future uncertainty and how these interpretations shape migration and non-migration strategies. Using a qualitative narrative inquiry approach, data were collected through in-depth interviews, social observation, and secondary sources. Twenty participants were interviewed, with seven informationrich cases selected for detailed narrative analysis after thematic saturation. Data were analyzed through open, axial, and selective coding. The findings show that migration decisions are not determined solely by economic factors. Instead, future uncertainty shapes how young people evaluate risks, opportunities, and possible life trajectories. Three orientations emerged: Future Mobility Seekers, who view migration as a route to economic security; Future Explorers, who remain flexible and adaptive; and Future Stabilizers, who prefer staying to reduce risk. Across these orientations, migration and non-migration represent alternative strategies for managing uncertainty. Aspirations are predominantly pragmatic, emphasizing stable employment, secure income, housing, and family well-being, while environmental concerns are generally secondary to economic security.

title: Virtual-Institution Forms: The Firm as a Nexus of Intellectual Assets

detail.title: Virtual-Institution Forms: The Firm as a Nexus of Intellectual Assets

publicationDetails.detailsText: published with the 1997 Research in Marketing, Volume 13 Issue 4, 09/1997, pp. 157-183, Virtual-institution forms: The firm as a nexus of intellectual assets, author Olsen, Cyrus P

detail.abstract: This work examines the nature of firm boundaries. It suggests that, while the transaction-cost paradigm is useful, it is limited in its ability to predict the boundaries of a firm at any given point in time. An extension of the transaction-cost logic is used to suggest that firm boundaries are a "transaction-state" dependent set of governance structures. This implies that a firm's boundaries have two key characteristics that are neglected by transaction-cost theory. First, the transaction-by-transaction nature of economic exchange is proposed as the true basis for defining a set of economic transactions as the boundary of the firm. Secondly, in the tradition of resource dependence theory (Pfeffer & Salancik, 1978), it argues that firm boundaries at any given point in time are functionally defined rather than legally defined and therefore are state-dependent in a Markovian stochastic sense (Gillespie, 1992). This latter property suggests that firm boundaries are a set of individually structured economic transactions. They are "virtual," or "existing in effect or essence though not in actual fact or form" (American Heritage Dictionary, 1993) as time-determined effects. This is opposed to transaction-cost economics' view that firm boundaries are legal-facts rather than functional-effects. A decision heuristic is proposed for determining the transaction-cost minimizing structure for individual, state-dependent transactions. This heuristic is based upon an analysis of a transaction's required degree of asymmetric information and the expected net-present value of any individual transaction given that transaction's state.

title: Capital Pledgeability and Credit Misallocation
affiliations: Banque de France

detail.title: Capital Pledgeability and Credit Misallocation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Banque de France Working Paper No. 1058
publicationDetails.journalName: Banque de France Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper examines how heterogeneous capital pledgeability shapes capital allocation. I first document, using French firm-level data, that firms holding more pledgeable capital are structurally more leveraged and display greater sensitivity of investment to credit supply shocks. I then incorporate heterogeneous capital pledgeability into a general equilibrium model with collateral constraints. This feature creates sectoral capital misallocation: highpledgeability capital is less costly to accumulate and thus yields lower expected returns than low-pledgeability capital, both in steady state and in response to credit supply shocks. I estimate the model based on a simple distinction between commercial real estate and other types of capital goods, the former being more pledgeable. I then show that capital misallocation is substantial over the credit cycle. Because these capital goods are imperfect substitutes and firms face a unique interest rate, redistributive credit policies taxing debt issued by high-pledgeability firms while subsidizing that of less pledgeable firms raise welfare, particularly when implemented during a credit expansion.

title: Faster Trips, Changes to Tips? The Impact of Congestion Pricing on Ride-Hailing Services: Evidence From NYC

detail.title: Faster Trips, Changes to Tips? The Impact of Congestion Pricing on Ride-Hailing Services: Evidence From NYC
detail.abstract: Urban congestion imposes significant economic and environmental costs for cities. In response, many municipalities have implemented policies such as congestion pricing to discourage vehicle use in congested areas. This study examines the impact of congestion pricing on the car-hailing sector using a congestion pricing scheme implemented in New York City in 2025. Employing event study, Difference-in-Differences, and Regression Discontinuity Design approaches, this study investigates effects on rider and driver outcomes. The results show that the increase in fares resulting from the congestion charge has not led to statistically significant decreases in trip distances and riders' tipping propensity, while tip amounts have increased following the intervention, potentially due to improved perceived service quality from shorter travel times and percentage-based tipping options that translate higher fares into larger tips. The results also show that congestion pricing has reduced traffic congestion and trip completion times, with improvements extending beyond routes directly affected by the charge. However, passenger pickup times have not undergone a statistically significant reduction. These findings highlight broader effects of congestion pricing on ride-hailing markets beyond demand responses, providing policymakers with a nuanced perspective on these policies.

title: Expectation-Driven Inventories, Unexpected Inventories, and Business Cycles
affiliations: Tohoku Gakuin University

detail.title: Expectation-Driven Inventories, Unexpected Inventories, and Business Cycles

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because this study uses only publicly available aggregate data.

detail.abstract: The Bank of Japan's Tankan (Short-term Economic Survey of Enterprises in Japan) reports firms' assessments of current business conditions at the end of each quarter and their forecasts of business conditions one quarter ahead. This paper exploits the unique information structure of the Tankan to develop an identification strategy in which the identifying restrictions follow directly from the timing structure of the data, thereby identifying expectation-driven and unexpected inventory shocks. A striking finding is that expectation-driven inventory shocks have little effect on observed aggregate inventory investment despite generating immediate increases in output, investment, labor demand, and consumption, suggesting that stronger demand offsets planned inventory accumulation. By contrast, unexpected inventory shocks account for the vast majority of aggregate inventory fluctuations and affect output, investment, and labor demand with a lag and the opposite sign. Taken together, these findings highlight that inventory fluctuations are not merely passive buffers against business cycle fluctuations but also constitute an important propagation mechanism for macroeconomic dynamics.

title: The Economics of Feng Shui: A Theory of Culturally Transmitted beliefs in Asset Markets
affiliations: Columbia University

detail.title: The Economics of Feng Shui: A Theory of Culturally Transmitted beliefs in Asset Markets
detail.abstract: When can a belief with no objective payoff consequences become permanently embedded in asset prices? I couple intergenerational preference transmission to a competitive asset market where an attribute yields utility only to those who believe it does; parents exert costly effort to pass belief or skepticism to their children. The attribute's price capitalizes the belief's future prevalence and feeds back on transmission. When the belief is rare, believers scarcely compete for the attribute and believing is nearly free, so transmission revives; when it is widespread, the premium taxes believing children, discouraging their parents from transmitting the belief, and enlarges the visible overpayment, mobilizing skeptical parents to transmit skepticism to their children, so the belief recedes. The market taxes the belief but cannot eliminate it: every equilibrium path converges to a unique, globally stable interior steady state with a permanent premium. Cultural parameters determine how many believe; the interest rate determines only what believing costs. Payoff-based selection alone would render premia transient, so their persistence among the native-born identifies the transmission mechanism itself. In extensions, cheaper supply-side accommodation of a belief spreads it, and verifying intermediaries capture the speculative component of its price. The framework rationalizes superstition premia in housing markets, its motivating application, and applies to any heritable taste attached to a tradable asset.

title: Beyond FICO: Behavioral Calibration of SME Cash Flows and the Future of Revenue-based Financing: Toward Financial Inclusion for Visionaries, Small Businesses, and the Vulnerable
affiliations: and Hitotsubashi University - Graduate School of International Corporate Strategy

detail.title: Beyond FICO: Behavioral Calibration of SME Cash Flows and the Future of Revenue-based Financing: Toward Financial Inclusion for Visionaries, Small Businesses, and the Vulnerable

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Yasuhiro Kawakami is the CEO of Pensata, Inc., which commercializes the BYLAS Score and related technologies (patent pending). Ryosuke Fujitani declares no competing interests.
